a2997.speaker: BONELA (Botswana Network on Ethics, Law and HIV/AIDS) (brief report, "BONELA's Reflections and Advocacy, Post-Workers' Day Commemoration in Ghanzi")
a2997.name: BONELA (Botswana Network on Ethics
a2997.title: Law and HIV/AIDS) (brief report, "BONELA's Reflections and Advocacy, Post-Workers' Day Commemoration in Ghanzi")
a2997.speech: "As part of its commemoration, BONELA remembered over 10,000 civil society employees who lost their jobs due to funding cuts by the US government," said the BONELA brief.

a2997.speaker: BONELA (Botswana Network on Ethics, Law and HIV/AIDS)
a2997.name: BONELA (Botswana Network on Ethics
a2997.title: Law and HIV/AIDS)
a2997.speech: Called on the Botswana Government and its development partners "to prioritise workers' rights to livelihoods and income" and reaffirmed "its commitment - together with state actors, trade unions, civil society, and international partners - to make workers' rights a lived reality in Botswana".

a2997.speaker: BONELA (Botswana Network on Ethics, Law and HIV/AIDS)
a2997.name: BONELA (Botswana Network on Ethics
a2997.title: Law and HIV/AIDS)
a2997.speech: Noted that the human rights advocacy organisation had joined the world in commemorating International Workers' Day, held under the theme "Workers' Rights Are Human Rights" ; "This theme is particularly relevant as it calls on all stakeholders to reflect on their roles in protecting, promoting and fulfilling workers' rights" ; said May 1st is more than a date: "It symbolises resistance, struggle, resilience and most importantly, solidarity. It honours the persistent fight for the 8-hour workday and the dignity that work as a right deserves."

a2997.speaker: BONELA (Botswana Network on Ethics, Law and HIV/AIDS)
a2997.name: BONELA (Botswana Network on Ethics
a2997.title: Law and HIV/AIDS)
a2997.speech: Said key emerging themes such as vulnerable conditions, gender wage gaps, and exploitation of domestic workers and migrant workers were tackled ; "Decent work is a cornerstone of human rights. Every worker - regardless of geography, industry, or sector - deserves the right to fair and dignified employment conditions and to speak up against abuse." ; "Beyond employment, universal social protection systems that build social justice are essential. Effective grievance and dispute resolution mechanisms, access to justice via credible dispute bodies, employers, and unions must collaborate to build inclusive, sustainable systems." ; "A strong call to action was given to informal sector workers - including domestic workers, agriculture labourers, street vendors, and others - whose labour sustains entire communities. Their rights and voices matter." ; "Ultimately, workers' rights are human rights. The fight for fair work is the fight for equality, for dignity and for justice."

a2997.speaker: Moeti Mohwasa, Minister of State President of Botswana (keynote address, as reported in the BONELA brief)
a2997.name: Moeti Mohwasa
a2997.title: Minister of State President of Botswana (keynote address, as reported in the BONELA brief)
a2997.speech: "In his remarks, he reaffirmed the government's commitment to promoting and upholding workers' rights." ; "He emphasised the historic alliance between the workers' movement and the current ruling party, dating back to its days in opposition. Minister Mohwasa expressed his expectation that this close relationship will continue and enable the government and workers to collaborate towards shared national goals."

a3031.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3031.name: Donald Trump
a3031.title: US President
a3031.speech: Hopes the Ukrainian conflict will be resolved within a year, otherwise there could be a third world war.

a3031.speaker: Zenon Mukongo Ngay, Permanent Representative of the DRC to the UN
a3031.name: Zenon Mukongo Ngay
a3031.title: Permanent Representative of the DRC to the UN
a3031.speech: Told Sputnik that Kinshasa is concerned about the situation with laboratories sponsored by the American USAID in the DRC.

a3031.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3031.name: Donald Trump
a3031.title: US President
a3031.speech: Stated that President Emmanuel Macron could travel to Washington as early as “Monday perhaps.”

a3031.speaker: Russian Ministry of Defence
a3031.name: Russian Ministry of Defence
a3031.speech: Said Russian air defences destroyed four Ukrainian drones overnight over Crimea and the Bryansk region.

a3031.speaker: Head of the Africa Partnership Department at the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3031.name: Head of the Africa Partnership Department at the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3031.speech: Told Sputnik that because of Western sanctions, Russia was unable in 2024 to send money for food aid to African countries such as Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger and Sudan.

a3068.speaker: Edouard Nyandwi, Director of Inland Transport (Burundi Ministry of Transport)
a3068.name: Edouard Nyandwi
a3068.title: Director of Inland Transport (Burundi Ministry of Transport)
a3068.speech: Indicated on Monday 16 June 2025 that the ministry in charge of transport has already begun awareness-raising on the use of electric vehicles, and that the programme of transition towards electric mobility is proving to be a sustainable solution ; confirms the shortage of public transport buses, in addition to the fuel problem, and says several projects are being implemented including the exemption on the importation of electric buses ; "We have begun awareness-raising on the use of electric vehicles. This programme of transition towards electric mobility is proving to be a sustainable solution. It responds not only to the fuel problem, but also to the conditions for protecting the environment and complying with anti-pollution measures as provided for by national and international laws."

a3068.speaker: Edouard Nyandwi, Director of Inland Transport (Burundi Ministry of Transport)
a3068.name: Edouard Nyandwi
a3068.title: Director of Inland Transport (Burundi Ministry of Transport)
a3068.speech: Reports that the government of Burundi has spent years with multiple exemption rights in this transport sector for entrepreneurs who import large public transport buses with more than thirty-nine passenger seats ; "The government has made it easy to import new right-hand buses with more than thirty-nine seats by removing the compulsory import taxes. It favours right-hand buses (steering wheel on the left and doors on the right) in order to combat the accidents that can be caused by the opening of doors and the exit of passengers according to the direction of travel in our highway code in Burundi."

a3068.speaker: Public transport users in Bujumbura
a3068.name: Public transport users in Bujumbura
a3068.speech: Complain that the lack of buses that is sometimes apparent at the parking areas is not only linked to the fuel problem.

a3068.speaker: Bus drivers (interviewed by Le Renouveau du Burundi)
a3068.name: Bus drivers (interviewed by Le Renouveau du Burundi)
a3068.speech: Say that the insufficiency of buses dates back to the withdrawal of old buses that could cause road accidents.

a3068.speaker: Charles Ntirampeba, Secretary General of Atrabu (Association of Transporters of Burundi)
a3068.name: Charles Ntirampeba
a3068.title: Secretary General of Atrabu (Association of Transporters of Burundi)
a3068.speech: Indicates that the Bujumbura city hall area has more than a thousand registered coaster buses still in service ; "Given the quota of 50 litres of diesel per bus per day, only about four hundred buses are served. You can see that the number served is less than half of the total number of buses. Sopebu (the Petroleum Company of Burundi) should increase the list to the maximum possible. When it serves even just eight hundred coaster buses per day, you will see a very noticeable change in the passenger queues because they are supported by the minibuses" ; states that the quota of 50 litres of diesel per day is not enough to cover fifteen round trips from the city centre to the assigned neighbourhood ; "The test week promised by Sopebu and the Bujumbura municipality to analyse and establish the truth or falsity of this argument did not take place, a month ago."

a3348.speaker: Oleksandr Merezhko, chair of the Ukrainian parliament's foreign affairs committee
a3348.name: Oleksandr Merezhko
a3348.title: chair of the Ukrainian parliament's foreign affairs committee
a3348.speech: "We'll see very soon the serious consequences — dangerous consequences," he told the BBC; said the pause could start having an impact on the ground as soon as "in the coming days." ; "When we are in desperate need of American weaponry, of American support... [it] looks like siding with Russia" to end it now. ; "I'm appealing to Mr Trump not to play with these dangerous issues because we're talking about lives."

a3348.speaker: Oleksandr Merezhko, chair of the Ukrainian parliament's foreign affairs committee
a3348.name: Oleksandr Merezhko
a3348.title: chair of the Ukrainian parliament's foreign affairs committee
a3348.speech: Said the decision also shone "a new light" on the Oval Office spat on Friday between Zelensky and the US president and vice-president, which he called "an attempt to find justification" to stop the military aid. ; "It was a show, you know, deliberately played."

a3348.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
a3348.name: White House official (anonymous)
a3348.speech: Told the BBC's US news partner, CBS, that its reason for pausing and reviewing military aid was to "ensure that it is contributing to a solution." ; "The President has been clear that he is focused on peace. We need our partners to be committed to that goal as well."

a3348.speaker: Denys Shmyhal, Prime Minister of Ukraine
a3348.name: Denys Shmyhal
a3348.title: Prime Minister of Ukraine
a3348.speech: Said his country was still willing to cooperate with the US, and reiterated Kyiv's "gratefulness" to Washington for their support to date.

a3348.speaker: US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky
a3348.name: US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky

a3348.speaker: Some Ukrainian MPs
a3348.name: Some Ukrainian MPs
a3348.speech: Have come out to call the decision "disastrous."

a3348.speaker: JD Vance, US Vice-President
a3348.name: JD Vance
a3348.title: US Vice-President
a3348.speech: Said he saw "big problems" with accusations that Trump was on Russian President Vladimir Putin's side, when asked during an interview on Monday; said people had to accept that Trump is "not just assuming that everything the Russians tell him is true."

a3382.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of Benin
a3382.name: Boni Yayi
a3382.title: President of Benin
a3382.speech: During the October visit to Benin of MCC CEO Johannes Daniel, repeatedly expressed the wish that the MCC would be indulgent enough to grant Benin a second compact.

a3382.speaker: Board of Directors of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3382.name: Board of Directors of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3382.speech: Has just renewed the compact programme for Benin for a further five years.

a3392.speaker: Barre Hilowle Mohamed, 64-year-old donkey cart driver in Baidoa displacement camp
a3392.name: Barre Hilowle Mohamed
a3392.title: 64-year-old donkey cart driver in Baidoa displacement camp
a3392.speech: "Our better off neighbours sometimes help us by giving us food. When they see we have not cooked anything at night, they assist us saying here is somehting you can cook tonight. That's how we are living now. If we get a few pieces of bread during the day, that's what we sleep on," he said ; "The biggest challenge we face is unemployment. The marketplace where we used to work has changed as people use tuk-tuks instead of our donkey carts. Even the people we used to rent the donkey carts from can't help us now," he said.

a3392.speaker: Mursal Hassan Ibrahim, donkey cart driver in Bula-nurio camp, Baidoa
a3392.name: Mursal Hassan Ibrahim
a3392.title: donkey cart driver in Bula-nurio camp, Baidoa
a3392.speech: "The worry we have now is if our lives continue like this, our children won't get an education, and as we've lost our jobs, we can't support our wives and children," he said. "I fear that our lives will become even more difficult and we'll be in deep trouble." ; "I owe three months' worth of rental for the donkey cart hire, which was one dollar a day. I thought this month would be better for me, but the debt has accumulated to three months so that's $90. I also owe $170 to a shop where I used to get food," he said.

a3392.speaker: Ali Isaaq Dahir, chairman of a committee representing 101 camps around Baidoa
a3392.name: Ali Isaaq Dahir
a3392.title: chairman of a committee representing 101 camps around Baidoa
a3392.speech: According to him, around 300 families who depended on income from donkey carts have been put out of work by the switch to tuk-tuks; he added that the traditional way of communities helping one another out had been greatly eroded by aid cuts and the economic downturn and loss of casual jobs ; "People used to help each other. If a donkey-cart owner managed to work that day, he would contribute, and we would identify any family in trouble within the camps so the community would make sure that household had food to cook. But now, even that kind of helping has stopped. The very person who used to help others is now struggling himself," Dahir said.

a3392.speaker: Ali Isaaq Dahir, chairman of a committee representing 101 camps around Baidoa
a3392.name: Ali Isaaq Dahir
a3392.title: chairman of a committee representing 101 camps around Baidoa
a3392.speech: Said the committee had informed the South West State administration and humanitarian organisations of the crisis in the camps, as new families continued to arrive daily, displaced by conflict and drought, further stretching scarce resources.

a3397.speaker: Ross Douthat and other conservative commentators, The New York Times
a3397.name: Ross Douthat and other conservative commentators
a3397.title: The New York Times
a3397.speech: A growing number of conservative commentators like Ross Douthat in The New York Times publicly applauded his transformation into a president with iron and steel in his body, morphing into Bush III.

a3397.speaker: Mitt Romney, Republican presidential hopeful
a3397.name: Mitt Romney
a3397.title: Republican presidential hopeful
a3397.speech: "President Obama has thrown Israel under the bus. He has disrespected Israel and undermined its ability to negotiate peace."

a3397.speaker: Tim Pawlenty, former Minnesota governor and Republican presidential hopeful
a3397.name: Tim Pawlenty
a3397.title: former Minnesota governor and Republican presidential hopeful
a3397.speech: Chipped in that Obama's position was a "disaster waiting to happen", adding, "at this time of upheaval in the Middle East, it's never been more important for America to stand strong for Israel and for a united Jerusalem."

a3397.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel
a3397.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a3397.title: Prime Minister of Israel
a3397.speech: Netanyahu's response, initially at least, was pretty truculent as well, saying he "expects to hear" a rethink from Obama and implying - well, more like saying - that Israeli politicians know more about their country's security needs than any US president; after the two leaders' Friday meeting, Netanyahu eventually put a slightly different spin on things, saying their talks revealed "differences" rather than equalling a major split between two close allies and friends.

a3397.speaker: Administration official (anonymous), quoted by The New York Times
a3397.name: Administration official (anonymous)
a3397.title: quoted by The New York Times
a3397.speech: "That was Bibi over the top," an administration official said (on) Saturday, referring to Mr. Netanyahu. "That's not how you address the president of the United States."

a3397.speaker: Jeffrey Goldberg, columnist with The Atlantic Monthly
a3397.name: Jeffrey Goldberg
a3397.title: columnist with The Atlantic Monthly
a3397.speech: Wrote: "So Netanyahu 'expects' to hear this from the president of the United States? And if President Obama doesn't walk back the speech, what will Netanyahu do? Will he cut off Israeli military aid to the US? Will he cease to fight for the U.S. in the United Nations, and in the many international forums that treat Israel as a pariah? I don't like this word, 'expect.'"

a3397.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States (State Department speech)
a3397.name: Barack Obama
a3397.title: President of the United States (State Department speech)
a3397.speech: Delineated his administration's goals in the Middle East, laying it out cleanly that the US position is peace between Israel and the Palestinians will be defined on the basis of the pre-1967 border, albeit with adjustments for security, and that the status of Jerusalem and the fate of the Palestinian refugees are matters to be settled later; he also set out the view that the Palestinians must be prepared to negotiate through to a settlement and that all groups must eschew the violence that has wracked the region.

a3397.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States (AIPAC convention speech)
a3397.name: Barack Obama
a3397.title: President of the United States (AIPAC convention speech)
a3397.speech: "Let me repeat what I actually said on Thursday, not what I was reported to have said." He argued: "The United States believes that negotiations should result in two states, with permanent Palestinian borders with Israel, Jordan, and Egypt, and permanent Israeli borders with Palestine. The borders of Israel and Palestine should be based on the 1967 lines with mutually agreed swaps, so that secure and recognised borders are established for both states." ; "Since my position has been misrepresented several times, let me reaffirm what '1967 lines with mutually agreed swaps' means. By definition, it means that the parties themselves - Israelis and Palestinians - will negotiate a border that is different than the one that existed on June 4, 1967. It is a well-known formula to all who have worked on this issue for a generation. It allows the parties themselves to account for the changes that have taken place over the last 44 years. There was nothing particularly original in my proposal. This basic framework for negotiations has long been the basis for discussions among the parties, including previous U.S. administrations." ; "I know very well that the easy thing to do, particularly for a president preparing for re-election, is to avoid any controversy." Obama added, "I don't need Rahm to tell me that." ; he had already told Netanyahu that, "I believe that the current situation in the Middle East does not allow for procrastination. I also believe that real friends talk openly and honestly with one another."

a3397.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States (AIPAC convention speech, on Iran and Syria)
a3397.name: Barack Obama
a3397.title: President of the United States (AIPAC convention speech, on Iran and Syria)
a3397.speech: "You also see our commitment to our shared security in our determination to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons... Its illicit nuclear program is just one challenge that Iran poses. As I said on Thursday, the Iranian government has shown its hypocrisy by claiming to support the rights of protesters while treating its own people with brutality. Moreover, Iran continues to support terrorism across the region, including providing weapons and funds to terrorist organizations. So we will continue to work to prevent these actions, and will stand up to groups like Hezbollah who exercise political assassination, and seek to impose their will through rockets and car bombs."

a3397.speaker: George Mitchell, former US special envoy to the Middle East, on ABC TV's "This Week"
a3397.name: George Mitchell
a3397.title: former US special envoy to the Middle East, on ABC TV's "This Week"
a3397.speech: Told Christiane Amanpour that: "I don't believe it is threatening Israel. ... A major objective of this initiative, among others, is to prevent a disaster for Israel from occurring at the UN General Assembly in September, when the Palestinians have said they will seek a unilateral declaration of statehood. ... [I]t's indisputable that we have not made as much progress [on Middle East peace] as we would have liked. ... [T]here's another definition of insanity, and that's to give up on a valid goal because you've gotten discouraged and you can't succeed."

a3397.speaker: Lee Rosenberg, AIPAC president
a3397.name: Lee Rosenberg
a3397.title: AIPAC president
a3397.speech: Introduced Obama with a guaranteed applause line: "Thank you, Mr. President, for ridding the world of Osama bin Laden."

a3397.speaker: Analysts (unnamed)
a3397.name: Analysts (unnamed)
a3397.speech: The kind of money - a billion or two - being talked about for the democracy development fund is nowhere near enough to provide the support needed, say analysts; his critics argue that Obama is trying to build democratic societies and economies on the cheap.

a3397.speaker: The New York Times
a3397.name: The New York Times
a3397.speech: Reported on Sunday the White House's response to Netanyahu's remarks, quoting an administration official.

a3463.speaker: Teboho Kobeli, founder of Afri-Expo Textiles (Lesotho)
a3463.name: Teboho Kobeli
a3463.title: founder of Afri-Expo Textiles (Lesotho)
a3463.speech: Could barely disguise his distress as he told the BBC about the impact of potentially losing a huge chunk of the US market because the prices of his goods will have to increase; described Thursday as a “terrible” and “devastating” day for people involved in Lesotho's textile sector.

a3463.speaker: South Africa's foreign and trade ministers (joint statement)
a3463.name: South Africa's foreign and trade ministers (joint statement)
a3463.speech: “The reciprocal tariffs effectively nullify the preferences that sub-Saharan Africa countries enjoy under Agoa,” South Africa's foreign and trade ministers said in a joint statement on Friday.

a3463.speaker: Korir Sing'oei, Kenya's Principal Secretary for Foreign Affairs
a3463.name: Korir Sing'oei
a3463.title: Kenya's Principal Secretary for Foreign Affairs
a3463.speech: “It is our considered view that until the law lapses end of September 2025 or unless repealed earlier by Congress, the new tariffs imposed by President Trump will, in any event, still not be immediately applicable,” he said in a statement.

a3463.speaker: Kenya (government position)
a3463.name: Kenya (government position)
a3463.speech: Kenya has tried to put a brave face on the issue, saying that as it was not hit as hard as other textile exporters, such as Vietnam and Sri Lanka, it would still have a competitive advantage.

a3463.speaker: Mukhisa Kituyi, former secretary-general of the UN Conference on Trade and Development and former Kenyan trade minister
a3463.name: Mukhisa Kituyi
a3463.title: former secretary-general of the UN Conference on Trade and Development and former Kenyan trade minister
a3463.speech: Says that if nothing changes, “a tariff of 50% sounds like a death knell to the Agoa manufacturing in Lesotho” ; argues that, as witnessed with the aid cuts, arguing about the human impact or fairness will not fly in the current set-up, in the face of “disruptive populism and post-fact, post-truth society” ; thinks countries like Kenya, with new tariffs set at 10%, could still try to hold ground in the US market, with exporters and their American importers negotiating how to absorb the new taxes without raising prices for the consumer too much ; says he has seen first-hand the effort that goes into “fine-tuning these processes” to create a “shared benefit from stable, predictable rules-based trading,” but reckons such agreements are now “hostage to the wishes of the dominant political group in America.”

a3463.speaker: World Bank (2018 report)
a3463.name: World Bank (2018 report)
a3463.speech: In 2018, the World Bank modelled a scenario where Lesotho experienced the sudden loss of Agoa privileges and found that the impact would “reach 1% of GDP” within two years; the report concluded that the impact on welfare would be “dramatic.”

a3463.speaker: Michelle Gavin, senior fellow for Africa policy studies at the Council on Foreign Relations
a3463.name: Michelle Gavin
a3463.title: senior fellow for Africa policy studies at the Council on Foreign Relations
a3463.speech: Said the way the new tariffs had been calculated “makes no sense at all” to economists, and that it is difficult to see “any kind of clear strategy or intention” from the Trump administration so far ; warns that the decisions will only exacerbate the loss of American influence in Africa, with China, already the continent's biggest trading partner, able to take further advantage: “It looks like a withdrawal, an ignoring of an entire huge region of the world” ; says that, coming shortly after the Trump administration severely pared back USAID, America appears to be “destroying its own instruments of influence with abandon now.”

a3492.speaker: Will Stevens, U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a3492.name: Will Stevens
a3492.title: U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a3492.speech: Has expressed satisfaction over the launch of the Refrigerated Aggregation Center, a solar-powered cold storage facility in Enugu; thanked the project's many public and private sector stakeholders, including the Enugu State Marketing Company, Enugu State Polytechnic Iwollo, and all the smallholder farmers, who have contributed to the success of this project ; commended Uzo, one of 12,000 Nigerians who have participated in U.S. government exchange programs, for participating in the development of the project: "It is so cool to see how Uzo used his 6-week exchange experience at the University of Nevada-Reno to forge connections that are now benefiting his local community. Since he returned to Nigeria in 2018, he stayed in contact with the university's college of business, leading them to provide technical and business advisory support to launch this project."

a3492.speaker: Will Stevens, U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a3492.name: Will Stevens
a3492.title: U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a3492.speech: "In Nigeria, as in other emerging economies, infrastructure is critical to driving inclusive and sustainable economic growth and development. Infrastructure connects workers to good jobs; allows businesses to grow and thrive, and creates opportunities for all segments of society, including underserved communities. Meeting infrastructure needs of public and private financing op across Nigeria requires a wide range tions. No one country can go it alone and that is why the United States is invested in Nigeria's economic success through private sector engagement coupled with targeted government support."

a3492.speaker: Will Stevens, U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a3492.name: Will Stevens
a3492.title: U.S. Consul General in Lagos
a3492.speech: "The solar-powered cold storage facility being commissioned today is just one example of how the U.S. government is partnering with federal and state government agencies and businesses to promote food security in Nigeria. Last month, alongside our partners in the Nigerian agricultural value chain, we launched the U.S. government's Global Food Security Strategy Country Plan for Nigeria that aims to boost agriculture productivity and drive agriculture-led economic growth."

a3518.speaker: Nigerien authorities
a3518.name: Nigerien authorities
a3518.speech: According to the authorities of Niger, this initiative will create new jobs, stimulate the local economy and improve the population's quality of life.

a3542.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3542.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a3542.title: President of Malawi
a3542.speech: Expressed concern over rising cases of political violence in the country ahead of the September 16, 2025 Local Government, Parliamentary and Presidential Elections, and said the incident at Mponela Trading Centre in Dowa District should not be tolerated in any form, especially in politics, as no individual or political party is superior to others: “Yesterday, disturbing reports came from Dowa and Mzimba, where people failed to engage in peaceful politics, resulting in violence and bloodshed. People were not in their right minds, but simply because of politics—rejecting election outcomes and resorting to fighting, even [some people] ending up in the hospital. Should our nurses in hospitals be burdened with such matters? That kind of behaviour is not acceptable; it is destroying our country” ; further said Malawians had become accustomed to violence, which is why in situations involving shortages—whether of chairs, fuel, sugar, fertiliser, maize or even votes—people resort to fighting instead of following due process, said this is because selfishness has taken root in the country, and urged the public not to burden nurses with these issues.

a3542.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3542.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a3542.title: President of Malawi
a3542.speech: Said his government remains committed to supporting and improving the welfare of nurses, which is why it has promoted and recruited more nurses: “My goal is to ensure that we take care of our nurses in several ways. Firstly, my government is focusing on nursing education making sure that we support many young people who aspire to join the profession by giving them opportunities to acquire the necessary skills. We are committed to supporting nursing schools.”

a3542.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a3542.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a3542.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a3542.speech: Said that the Ministry will continue supporting nurses and that the government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Israeli government to recruit unemployed nurses in Malawi: “You have seen that government has been making recruitments and promoting nurses. As government, we will continue to support efforts to improve healthcare service delivery in Malawi” ; further called on those responsible for recruitment and promotions to do so fairly, without discrimination based on region or district of origin.

a3542.speaker: Shouts Simeza, President of the National Organisation of Nurses and Midwives (NONM)
a3542.name: Shouts Simeza
a3542.title: President of the National Organisation of Nurses and Midwives (NONM)
a3542.speech: Said caring for nurses and midwives has the potential to improve the country’s economy and appealed to the President to ensure health workers are equipped with the resources they need: “These nurses are ready and capable. They understand the health profile of Malawi, the disease burdens and trends, and the healthcare delivery system. They are the largest segment of the health workforce and work in collaboration with the entire system. They are an essential investment for Malawi to combat both communicable and non-communicable diseases and to achieve universal health coverage. They must be available and responsive to emerging health needs.”

a3542.speaker: Shouts Simeza, President of the National Organisation of Nurses and Midwives (NONM)
a3542.name: Shouts Simeza
a3542.title: President of the National Organisation of Nurses and Midwives (NONM)
a3542.speech: Called on the government to continue supporting nursing education, especially after the withdrawal of USAID support: “This situation has resulted in massive dropouts, colleges struggling to survive, and needy but deserving students being left behind. There is inadequate support for learners limited clinical supervision, insufficient teaching equipment in hospitals, and a lack of proper accommodation during clinical placements, exposing students to various forms of abuse.”

a3570.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a3570.title: president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.speech: On the signing of the 2nd MCA Compact: “I would first like to say that this signing is a complete success. We must salute the work that has been done, and I say congratulations to the President of the Republic for his leadership. You know under what conditions and why we were suspended... We must salute the work of the MCC team and of the MCA-Benin team, on which the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin is represented.” ; “There is no particular expectation. The second compact is simply the continuation of the first... That prepared the ground for the second compact, whose distinctive feature is essentially focused on the energy sector... with the particularity of bringing the Beninese and international private sector into production.” ; “The principle of this second compact launched a call for ideas from users, and so my own group, CDPA-Agrisatch, was approached and we made proposals on how we can contribute to producing solar energy and biomass-based energy... Energy is the engine of development, and without energy you cannot achieve development, still less industrial development.”

a3570.speaker: Patrice Talon, President of the Republic of Benin
a3570.name: Patrice Talon
a3570.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a3570.speech: Says that in view of Benin's needs projected over time, the country must achieve 1,000 MW (of electrical capacity).

a3570.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a3570.title: president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.speech: On partnership with American business: “The presentation records that the compact amounts to about 411 million dollars. These resources will produce 78 MW of electrical energy... And there is even provision inside it for a cost-sharing fund... So it serves as a catalyst to go and seek other investments.” ; “Even before we went there, we had begun a discussion with the officials of the [US] Chamber's Africa department... That is how we discovered the CIP, which is a structure that supports the development of businesses internationally... We plan to sign a partnership with this structure shortly.” ; “The weakness of francophone countries is that we do not have big economic exchange links with the United States. The United States Chamber of Commerce can serve as a support point to strengthen this emerging Africa. We must work to improve our standards in terms of entrepreneurship, to develop our companies to be competitive at the international level.”

a3570.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a3570.title: president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.speech: On AGOA: “AGOA is a law that opens the American market to nearly 6,000 African products. Benin was chosen to take part in it. The first approach of the Chamber's new team is to diagnose the result of this AGOA... There is nevertheless one Beninese company that works with the United States and has stayed the course. It is Natura... But as for everything textile, we have not managed it. Lolo Andoche, who has made enormous efforts, is not yet at the level... what the American market demands... is mass production. Volume is needed.” ; “Over these 15 years the Chamber has worked to meet AGOA's requirements, but it has not worked miracles beyond measure. Fifteen years are in any case not enough to bring oneself up to American standards, to enter into the Anglo-Saxon mentality of entrepreneurship.” ; “Take our sugarloaf pineapples: do they comply with American phytosanitary standards?... We have a great deal of wealth that AGOA can awaken, but we must be in step with American standards.”

a3570.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a3570.title: president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.speech: On the public-private partnership: “We must salute the dialogue that was begun in October 2012 but which did not go to the very end of its completion because there was a bit of exclusion inside it... We came out of those general assemblies with a platform that brings everyone together without exclusion... The public-private partnership (PPP) can only be strengthened. But there was also the problem of the legal framework... The private sector does not feel secure in these investments and is proposing texts. Work has been done, which is now at the level of Parliament... We must create Beninese champions further... The other element is the strengthening of an operational justice system for the cause of the PPP.”

a3570.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.name: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi
a3570.title: president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
a3570.speech: On what he expects from government on the business climate: “What we expect from the government is very simple. First, more consideration for the one who undertakes, I mean the business leader whatever his size... What we owe the State is to create favourable conditions as regards the factors of production and raw materials. We must accompany the government so that the government accompanies us. We are not going to ask for exemptions on everything from a State that needs a fiscal budget in order to work.” ; “The only thing lacking today is a fruitful dialogue between the public sector and the private sector represented by a non-exclusive platform. I would like to make an appeal to the President of the Republic to kindly ensure that this platform becomes a reality before his departure. It will be an important element of his legacy... Beninese people must learn to come together in order to win.”

a3757.speaker: Abdourahamane Diallo, 26-year-old defendant
a3757.name: Abdourahamane Diallo
a3757.title: 26-year-old defendant
a3757.speech: At the bar denied the rape charges against him, maintaining that it was at the request of the girl, who is his “girlfriend”, that they filmed their sexual intercourse, and that it was the girl, not wanting a marriage, who asked him to share the video ; “She is my girlfriend. One day she told me she was getting married soon. But she let me know that she did not like her suitor. And that it was her parents who were forcing her to accept this marriage. One day she came to my house with the number of the elder brother of her fiancé who lives in the United States, and asked me to film our lovemaking so that she could send it to her fiancé's elder brother for the sole purpose of cancelling the marriage, which had already been set. So to say that I raped her and filmed her against her will is not true. It is with her consent that we did all this.”

a3757.speaker: Representative of the public prosecutor's office (ministère public)
a3757.name: Representative of the public prosecutor's office (ministère public)
a3757.speech: In his submissions recalled that the accused had admitted having had sexual relations with the victim, who is a minor, and also admitted having filmed and sent the images; he therefore asked the court to find Abdourahamane Diallo guilty and to sentence him to 5 years of criminal imprisonment.

a3757.speaker: Lawyer for the civil party
a3757.name: Lawyer for the civil party
a3757.speech: Endorsed the prosecutor's submissions while asking the judge to follow them; he also pleaded for the accused to be ordered to pay 200 million Guinean francs in damages.

a3757.speaker: Defence counsel
a3757.name: Defence counsel
a3757.speech: Argued that the girl was 20 years old at the time of the events, contrary to what is being said, and that it was at the girl's request that his client filmed and sent the videos; he asked the court for the outright dismissal of the case against his client.

a3757.speaker: Court of First Instance of Dixinn (ruling)
a3757.name: Court of First Instance of Dixinn (ruling)
a3757.speech: In its deliberation declared Abdourahamane Diallo guilty of rape of a minor and of endangering life; as punishment he was sentenced to 3 years in prison and to the payment of 50 million GNF in damages.

a3874.speaker: Council of Ministers' 100-day macroeconomic performance review (Ethiopia)
a3874.name: Council of Ministers' 100-day macroeconomic performance review (Ethiopia)
a3874.speech: The projection that Ethiopia's economy will expand by 10.2 percent was presented during the review, which examined global economic trends, Ethiopia’s quarterly economic outcomes, and the nation’s medium-term growth outlook. According to the review, Ethiopia maintained robust growth in the previous fiscal year, registering 9.2 percent GDP expansion, driven by steady gains in agriculture (7.3%), industry (13%), and services (7.5%).

a4020.speaker: Tiffany Miller, acting deputy chief of mission of the US embassy
a4020.name: Tiffany Miller
a4020.title: acting deputy chief of mission of the US embassy
a4020.speech: Explained at the official handover ceremony that the mission of the OHDACA is to fund humanitarian assistance activities and enhance the capacity of partner nations to prepare for and respond to humanitarian crises ; “This fully equipped five-bed intensive care unit is a mobile and self-sufficient system. It provides the ministry of health and social services with a resource that can be used to support the local population in Walvis Bay or can be disassembled, transported and reassembled in a matter of days to respond to a crisis in the most remote locations” ; explained that the unit is self-sufficient with dual generator power, water and sewage systems, and air conditioning, allowing it to operate autonomously in the field ; “It is also stocked with N$600 000 worth of medicine to ensure the ICU is immediately ready for operations. A team of Namibian personnel, including doctors and nurses from the ministry, were trained in all aspects of the ICU set-up as well as the individual pieces of medical equipment within the ICU.”

a4020.speaker: Tiffany Miller, acting deputy chief of mission of the US embassy
a4020.name: Tiffany Miller
a4020.title: acting deputy chief of mission of the US embassy
a4020.speech: Further stated that this is the first of four donations that will be installed across Namibia in the coming months: “These donations include a second five-bed ICU in Otjiwarongo, as well as two field hospitals in Outapi and Katima Mulilo, each including a 30-bed negative pressure isolation facility and a UN Level I Urgent Care Clinic. These donations will total over N$128 million in value and represent the largest single DoD humanitarian assistance donation to the Namibian people to date.”

a4020.speaker: Ben Nangombe, executive director of the health ministry
a4020.name: Ben Nangombe
a4020.title: executive director of the health ministry
a4020.speech: Explained that the addition of this state-of-the-art mobile intensive care unit comes at a crucial time as the ministry is enhancing capacity at public health facilities nationwide to provide services to the people ; “Following Covid-19, we had about 23 ICU beds in Onandjokwe, Oshakati, Katutura Hospital and Windhoek Central Hospital. There were no other ICU beds in state health facilities, and we realised that there was a serious gap.” ; said the ministry, in order to address the shortfall in ICU beds at all 34 district hospitals, is going to get ICU capacity funded by the Namibian government ; “By the completion of this project, we will have no fewer than 200 ICU beds. We know that we need to bring services closer to the people, and we are truly grateful for all the support we are receiving to increase that capacity.”

a4020.speaker: Ben Nangombe, executive director of the health ministry
a4020.name: Ben Nangombe
a4020.title: executive director of the health ministry
a4020.speech: Explained that in terms of Walvis Bay, it will not only have ICU capacity funded by the government but will also have an additional mobile ICU facility: “In recent years, the demand for ICU services has grown significantly. Many patients requiring intensive care have had to be transferred to Windhoek. The long distances present considerable risk. The long-distance transfers not only strain our healthcare resources but also place additional stress on patients and their families. The establishment of a fully equipped ICU facility here in Walvis Bay will mitigate these challenges, ensuring that critical care is accessible in a timely manner.”

a4089.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a4089.name: Emmanuel Macron
a4089.title: President of France
a4089.speech: Speaking during the Council of Ministers about the operations carried out by Israel in the Middle East, said on Tuesday that "Mr Netanyahu must not forget that his country was created by a decision of the UN" ; "This is not the time to break free from UN decisions," he again stressed on Tuesday in the Council of Ministers ; Insisted last week that halting exports of weapons used by Israel in the Gaza Strip and in Lebanon was the only way to end these wars.

a4089.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister (statement issued by his office)
a4089.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a4089.title: Israeli Prime Minister (statement issued by his office)
a4089.speech: "A reminder to the president of France: it was not the UN resolution that established the State of Israel, but rather the victory obtained in the war of independence with the blood of heroic fighters, many of whom were survivors of the Holocaust - notably of the Vichy regime in France."

a4089.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister (statement issued by his office)
a4089.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a4089.title: Israeli Prime Minister (statement issued by his office)
a4089.speech: During their telephone exchange in the early evening, retorted "that he was opposed to a unilateral ceasefire, which would not change the security situation in Lebanon".

a4089.speaker: France (official position)
a4089.name: France (official position)
a4089.speech: Deemed it "completely unacceptable" that the blue helmets of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), which includes a French contingent, were being "selectively targeted by the Israeli armed forces", after several of them were wounded by Israeli fire in southern Lebanon.

a4147.speaker: Bloomberg (economic media outlet)
a4147.name: Bloomberg (economic media outlet)
a4147.speech: Reported that SpaceX and its investors recently agreed to buy up to $1.25 billion of the company’s shares, raising the value of the space firm to about $350 billion, and that this colossal transaction allowed Elon Musk’s fortune to increase by $50 billion, bringing it to $440 billion ; according to its data, the price of Tesla stock has also risen by more than 65% since the election of Donald Trump in early November.

a4147.speaker: US Federal Election Commission (FEC) figures
a4147.name: US Federal Election Commission (FEC) figures
a4147.speech: According to the FEC’s figures, Elon Musk became the largest political donor in recent American history, with more than $270 million paid out during the presidential campaign to support the Republican candidate.

a4147.speaker: CNews
a4147.name: CNews
a4147.speech: Cited as the source of the article.

a4257.speaker: Eskom and FFS Refiners (fuel supplier)
a4257.name: Eskom and FFS Refiners (fuel supplier)
a4257.speech: Have confirmed that a circulating voice note claiming load shedding is due to Eskom not paying a fuel supplier is fake news, and that Eskom is up to date with payments.

a4257.speaker: Mossel Bay Magistrate's Court (court ruling)
a4257.name: Mossel Bay Magistrate's Court (court ruling)
a4257.speech: Set aside interim protection orders and suspended arrest warrants against News24 journalists Karyn Maughan and Kelly Anderson.

a4257.speaker: Ezra Morrison, Magistrate
a4257.name: Ezra Morrison
a4257.title: Magistrate
a4257.speech: Obtained the orders, accusing the journalists of harassment for their reporting on her handling of a rape case involving the boy now accused of murdering Deveney Nel.

a4257.speaker: Fikile Mbalula, ANC secretary-general
a4257.name: Fikile Mbalula
a4257.title: ANC secretary-general
a4257.speech: Announced the ANC's new top six leadership team for KwaZulu-Natal, in Durban, after the party's poor showing in the province during the May general elections.

a4257.speaker: Lawsuit filed by USAID employees (court filing)
a4257.name: Lawsuit filed by USAID employees (court filing)
a4257.speech: Revealed the Trump administration's halt on USAID payments was so abrupt that some senior staff in South Africa were left without electricity; the lawsuit sought to reverse the Trump administration's decision to block payments and place employees on administrative leave, but was unsuccessful.

a4257.speaker: US government
a4257.name: US government
a4257.speech: Has promised to quickly settle outstanding payments, including unpaid living expenses for USAID employees overseas.

a4451.speaker: Malian transitional government (Council of Ministers of 5 March)
a4451.name: Malian transitional government (Council of Ministers of 5 March)
a4451.speech: Approved the ratification of the budget support agreement signed with the Qatar Fund for Development, providing 50 million dollars (about 31.447 billion CFA francs) for humanitarian aid, economic development and health.

a4451.speaker: Malian government
a4451.name: Malian government
a4451.speech: Gives assurances that these funds will be used rigorously and transparently, in order to guarantee concrete results on the ground.

a4466.speaker: Christopher Broughton, MCC Resident Representative in Benin
a4466.name: Christopher Broughton
a4466.title: MCC Resident Representative in Benin
a4466.speech: Stressed that the key to their success is the government's commitment through the board of directors of the entities known as “MCA”, which are responsible for administering MCC grant agreements, and also the professionalism, ethics and excellence of the Beninese who work for the MCA entities (MCA-Benin I, MCA-Benin II and MCA-Benin Regional).

a4466.speaker: Brian Shukan, United States Ambassador to Benin
a4466.name: Brian Shukan
a4466.title: United States Ambassador to Benin
a4466.speech: “Indeed, Benin is the only partner country in the world to be eligible for MCC assistance programmes and to have been developing or implementing an MCC grant agreement without interruption since 2004. This is an extraordinary achievement that no other country can match.” ; explained that the United States grants awarded by the MCC are interest-free gifts, allowing Benin to invest in water, health, education and other areas of public interest, and noted that since 2004 Benin has benefited from more than 540 billion CFA francs (900 million US dollars) under three MCC grant agreements, one of which is under way and targets the transport sector, administered by Beninese professionals to the strictest international standards.

a4466.speaker: Brian Shukan, United States Ambassador to Benin
a4466.name: Brian Shukan
a4466.title: United States Ambassador to Benin
a4466.speech: Thanked the government of Benin for its partnership with the United States of America in developing and implementing the grant agreements, whose impacts will be felt over several generations, and promised that the United States will continue to work with Benin to offer a bright future to the Beninese people.

a4466.speaker: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister in charge of Development and the Coordination of Government Action of Benin
a4466.name: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané
a4466.title: Minister in charge of Development and the Coordination of Government Action of Benin
a4466.speech: Expressed his full gratitude to the American government for the MCC's aid to Benin and acknowledged that thanks to these grants millions of people have been lifted out of poverty: “Benin is among the fortunate beneficiaries of these grants, and this continuously since 2006 through three grant agreements.” ; “In view of the three compacts from which Benin has benefited, one can affirm that MCC financing in Benin covers several dimensions, namely economic growth, poverty reduction, the strengthening of institutions, improved access to basic services and the strengthening of local capacities.”

a4466.speaker: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister in charge of Development and the Coordination of Government Action of Benin
a4466.name: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané
a4466.title: Minister in charge of Development and the Coordination of Government Action of Benin
a4466.speech: Indicated that Benin's eligibility with the MCC is linked to good performance in good governance, the creation of an environment favourable to private initiative, and the State's commitment to invest in human capital: “Benin has always worked to meet these conditions successfully, and successive governments have managed to satisfy the preconditions for the entry into force of each compact”, reiterating the government's commitment to maintain the momentum of reforms so that the American people may be proud of having contributed to Benin's development.

a4561.speaker: William Nyarko, lawyer, investigative journalist and Executive Director, Africa Center for International Law and Accountability
a4561.name: William Nyarko
a4561.title: lawyer, investigative journalist and Executive Director, Africa Center for International Law and Accountability
a4561.speech: Speaking to the media, said the field of investigative journalism must be supported to thrive to enable journalists whom the Constitution has given power, to expose through storytelling the abuse of power and State resources for accountability.

a4561.speaker: Zakaria Tanko Musah, Lecturer at the Ghana Institute of Journalism and member of the RTI Commission
a4561.name: Zakaria Tanko Musah
a4561.title: Lecturer at the Ghana Institute of Journalism and member of the RTI Commission
a4561.speech: Called on media house owners and news heads to invest in investigative journalism as it tends to be expensive and time-consuming but also gives media houses credibility ; added that when media houses use the RTI law to access information, it keeps the journalists in check, and helps them to conform to principles and procedures.

a4561.speaker: Alao Sunday Afolabi, Resident Program Director, International Republican Institute (IRI)
a4561.name: Alao Sunday Afolabi
a4561.title: Resident Program Director, International Republican Institute (IRI)
a4561.speech: Said in his speech that IRI had seen the need to train more journalists in the area of investigative journalism due to its immense impact on society ; said that as Ghana heads into an election in December there is the tendency for aspirants of political parties to illegally use public funds and resources for campaign and to misinform the public, and it places a responsibility on journalists to set the records straight with their news stories.

a4561.speaker: Rebecca Ekpe, Public Affairs Officer, Ghana Journalists Association
a4561.name: Rebecca Ekpe
a4561.title: Public Affairs Officer, Ghana Journalists Association
a4561.speech: Told the media that such training on equipping members with skills to improve on their craft as journalists goes to improve information dissemination to the public and guide them on the legal ways of seeking information, which is a major barrier in a journalist's line of activities when putting an investigative piece together.

a4627.speaker: Authorities in Tigray / Tigray rebels (statement)
a4627.name: Authorities in Tigray / Tigray rebels (statement)
a4627.speech: Said Sunday they were ready to take part in peace talks led by the African Union: “The government of Tigray is prepared to participate in a robust peace process under the auspices of the African Union.” ; “Furthermore we are ready to abide by an immediate and mutually agreed cessation of hostilities in order to create a conducive atmosphere.” ; the statement made no mention of any preconditions for talks, although it said it expected a “credible” peace process with “mutually acceptable” mediators as well as international observers.

a4627.speaker: Ethiopian government
a4627.name: Ethiopian government
a4627.speech: There was no immediate comment from the Ethiopian government, which has long insisted that any peace process must be brokered by the Addis Ababa-headquartered AU.

a4627.speaker: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a4627.name: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a4627.speech: Had until now vehemently opposed the role of the AU's Horn of Africa envoy Olusegun Obasanjo, protesting at his “proximity” to Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.

a4627.speaker: Debretsion Gebremichael, TPLF leader
a4627.name: Debretsion Gebremichael
a4627.title: TPLF leader
a4627.speech: Had earlier this month proposed a truce with four conditions including “unfettered humanitarian access” and the restoration of essential services in war-stricken Tigray; in a letter to UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, he had also called for the withdrawal of Eritrean forces from across Ethiopia, and for troops to pull out of western Tigray, a disputed region claimed by both Tigrayans and Amharas.

a4627.speaker: Moussa Faki Mahamat, AU Commission chief
a4627.name: Moussa Faki Mahamat
a4627.title: AU Commission chief
a4627.speech: Announced on Saturday that Obasanjo's mandate would be extended: “I reiterated my full confidence in him & encouraged his continued engagement with both parties & intl actors to work towards peace & reconciliation in Ethiopia & the region,” Faki said on Twitter after meeting Obasanjo; Faki also said he had held talks Saturday with visiting US envoy for the Horn of Africa, Mike Hammer.

a4627.speaker: Mike Hammer, US envoy for the Horn of Africa
a4627.name: Mike Hammer
a4627.title: US envoy for the Horn of Africa
a4627.speech: “May the parties in the conflict have the courage to choose talks over fighting, and participate in an African Union-led process that produces a lasting peace,” Hammer said in a new year's message for Ethiopians on Sunday.

a4627.speaker: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a4627.name: Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)
a4627.speech: Accused Ethiopian and Eritrean forces of launching a massive joint offensive on September 1.

a4627.speaker: United Nations
a4627.name: United Nations
a4627.speech: Had said on Thursday that the renewed fighting had forced a halt to desperately needed aid deliveries to Tigray, both by road and air.

a4627.speaker: UN humanitarian agency OCHA (situation report)
a4627.name: UN humanitarian agency OCHA (situation report)
a4627.speech: Said the violence was “already impacting the lives and livelihood of vulnerable people, including the delivery of lifesaving humanitarian assistance.”

a4659.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4659.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a4659.speech: says it regrets the American president’s decision and hopes that he will reverse the order he signed on January 20, only hours after his inauguration; the organization even says it is ready to engage in “constructive” dialogue with the Trump administration in order to maintain this partnership, for the benefit of the health and well-being of millions of people around the world.

a4659.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4659.name: Donald Trump
a4659.title: US President
a4659.speech: accused the WHO of “fraud” (“escroquerie”) on the question of vaccines against the Covid-19 pandemic; in 2020 he had already tried to withdraw his country from the organization, which he accused at the time of being controlled by China.

a5009.speaker: US National Institutes of Health (NIH) leaked memo dated 25 March (document)
a5009.name: US National Institutes of Health (NIH) leaked memo dated 25 March (document)
a5009.speech: Instructs grant management officers to hold “all [research] awards to entities located in South Africa”; states that it replaces a previous document sent on 13 February and explains which research grants to terminate; states that “additional guidance on awards to foreign entities is forthcoming” but “at this time” NIH institutes and centres should “hold all awards to entities located in South Africa” or countries considered of “particular concern” by the US state department, “state sponsors of terrorism”, “office of foreign assets control sanctions list” or “final rule restricting transfer of personal US data to countries of concern” ; says “it is the policy of the NIH not to prioritise diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) research programmes, gender identity, vaccine hesitancy, climate change or countries of concern, e.g. China or South Africa” ; gives grant staff five scenarios to respond to, including projects whose “sole purpose” relates to an area the NIH no longer “prioritises”, programmes that “may still be viable” if adjusted, grants that don’t “support any DEI activities”, “departmental authority terminations”, and “awards to entities in certain foreign countries”.

a5009.speaker: NIH cancellation/termination letters (documents)
a5009.name: NIH cancellation/termination letters (documents)
a5009.speech: Instructed South African universities and nonprofits to end their projects as they are based on “artificial and non-scientific categories”, “provide low returns on investment”, and “ultimately do not enhance health, lengthen life, or reduce illness” ; say recipients can appeal the NIH’s decision but simultaneously state “no corrective action [to the terminated programmes] is possible” and the “premise of this award is incompatible with agency priorities, and no modification of the project could align the project with agency priorities”.

a5009.speaker: National Institutes of Health (NIH)
a5009.name: National Institutes of Health (NIH)
a5009.speech: Bhekisisa has sent a request for comment to the NIH to confirm when, and if, the memo will come into effect; no response had been received at the time of publication.

a5009.speaker: World Report (research funding tracker)
a5009.name: World Report (research funding tracker)
a5009.speech: The NIH finances as much as 88% of biomedical research worldwide, according to the World Report, which tracks research funding.

a5009.speaker: Unnamed experts
a5009.name: Unnamed experts
a5009.speech: Some experts estimate that as much as 70% of South Africa’s medical research, or up to $400 million (about R7.2 billion), is funded through the NIH.

a5009.speaker: Linda-Gail Bekker, Desmond Tutu Foundation, University of Cape Town
a5009.name: Linda-Gail Bekker
a5009.title: Desmond Tutu Foundation, University of Cape Town
a5009.speech: Explains the uncertainty facing scientists: “Every day, every minute, you’re checking your grant on the NIH website, to see what might have happened. It makes it hard for scientists to roll out new study protocols, because there’s a sense of, ‘should we, shouldn’t we’.”

a5009.speaker: Linda-Gail Bekker, Desmond Tutu Foundation, University of Cape Town
a5009.name: Linda-Gail Bekker
a5009.title: Desmond Tutu Foundation, University of Cape Town
a5009.speech: Says South African universities will face devastating consequences if all NIH grants are cut: “As a result of research grants, universities receive administrative support through indirect costs, and our clinical trial sites build the next generation of HIV and TB researchers, as almost all our grants include positions for PhD and postdoc students” ; “It takes decades to build this infrastructure, it’s not something that can be rebuilt overnight” ; says HIV and TB infections, as well as deaths, will increase: “Viruses and bacteria constantly change. That’s why we need to consistently develop new medicines. We need to stay ahead of the pathogens. But if the funds are lacking, we have less ability to do so.”

a5009.speaker: President Donald Trump (executive order)
a5009.name: President Donald Trump (executive order)
a5009.speech: In early February, issued an executive order to halt foreign aid to South Africa, accusing the country of oppressing Afrikaners and “unjust and immoral practices that harm our nation [the US]”.

a5009.speaker: Mitchell Warren, executive director of the international health advocacy organisation Avac
a5009.name: Mitchell Warren
a5009.title: executive director of the international health advocacy organisation Avac
a5009.speech: Says President Trump does seem to single South Africa out: “It is very clear that the president is using budgets and terminations of previously agreed to programmes to redefine agendas, and in this case ones that defy science and are clearly political and ideological.”

a5009.speaker: Mitchell Warren, executive director of Avac
a5009.name: Mitchell Warren
a5009.title: executive director of Avac
a5009.speech: Warns that the speed at which the Trump administration moves with its cuts, and the abrupt manner in which they do this, will only increase uncertainty: “If these last eight weeks [since Trump’s inauguration] are anything to go by, the next three years and 10 months [will be] terrifying” ; “We’ve seen the systematic dismantling of some of the most critical infrastructure in global health, for research, for implementation and for policymaking. I worry that this has only just begun.”

a5009.speaker: The Washington Post
a5009.name: The Washington Post
a5009.speech: Reports that Jayanta Bhattacharya “rose to prominence as a vocal critic of the country’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic”, and reports on his confirmation hearing.

a5009.speaker: Jayanta Bhattacharya, newly confirmed NIH director
a5009.name: Jayanta Bhattacharya
a5009.title: newly confirmed NIH director
a5009.speech: Said during his confirmation hearing that the NIH was “at a crossroads”, saying the agency “oversaw a culture of cover-up, obfuscation and lack of tolerance for ideas that differed from theirs”.

a5009.speaker: Chris Beyrer, epidemiologist and director of the Duke Global Health Institute
a5009.name: Chris Beyrer
a5009.title: epidemiologist and director of the Duke Global Health Institute
a5009.speech: Told Bhekisisa at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in March: “One of the reasons South Africa has done so well with HIV research is because of the extraordinary depth of scientific talent. [Because of the HIV and TB research grants and USAID cuts in February] talented people may be worried about going into this field, and the talent and human resource is fundamental” ; said “we’re now worried about our international partnerships for collaborative research with countries like South Africa, and also China”.

a5009.speaker: The Lancet (editorial published 20 March)
a5009.name: The Lancet (editorial published 20 March)
a5009.speech: Cautions against “the emergence of widespread drug resistance”, “leading to a dramatic increase in infectious disease burden worldwide”.

a5009.speaker: ProPublica
a5009.name: ProPublica
a5009.speech: Reported on Monday that their journalists had seen internal NIH records stating that the grants funding research on the health effects of climate change will be terminated.

a5009.speaker: Science magazine
a5009.name: Science magazine
a5009.speech: Reported that they had confirmation from the NIH that it would end all Covid-19 research because it “will no longer waste billions of taxpayer dollars responding to a non-existent pandemic that Americans moved on from years ago”.

a5009.speaker: The New York Times
a5009.name: The New York Times
a5009.speech: Reported on Wednesday that the Trump administration will end its financial support for Gavi, which helps to vaccinate more than half the world’s children against some of the deadliest diseases, and that it will also cut funds for malaria; the Times got hold of a spreadsheet, sent to the US Congress, which details such cuts.

a5009.speaker: Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation
a5009.name: Mark Suzman
a5009.title: CEO of the Gates Foundation
a5009.speech: Said on Wednesday night on LinkedIn: “If true, and if Congress allows this to happen, the impacts will be devastating, including the possibility of hundreds of thousands, if not millions, of preventable deaths, especially among mothers and children. We are going to do everything possible to convince the Administration and the Congress to reverse these actions if true.”

a5011.speaker: Minister of Communications and Digital Transformation of Mozambique
a5011.name: Minister of Communications and Digital Transformation of Mozambique
a5011.speech: At the opening of the event, said that firm responses are needed to this type of crime [cybercrime].

a5011.speaker: Francisco Mabzaia, Chairman of the Board (PCA) of the Maputo Municipal Mobility and Parking Company (EMME)
a5011.name: Francisco Mabzaia
a5011.title: Chairman of the Board (PCA) of the Maputo Municipal Mobility and Parking Company (EMME)
a5011.speech: Says that of the roughly twenty million that would be ideal, the municipal company collects only four million from rotating parking, an amount insufficient to transform Maputo into a city of modern and intelligent systems.

a5011.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a5011.name: Pope Leo XIV
a5011.speech: Expresses solidarity with the victims of the earthquakes in Venezuela and appeals for the strengthening of international humanitarian aid to the populations affected by the tragedy.

a5011.speaker: Fishermen of Inhambane Bay
a5011.name: Fishermen of Inhambane Bay
a5011.speech: Acknowledge the increasingly sharp reduction in shellfish and point to the growing pressure exerted on coastal and marine ecosystems.

a5011.speaker: Residents of the village of Niarro, Natikiri neighbourhood, Nampula
a5011.name: Residents of the village of Niarro
a5011.title: Natikiri neighbourhood, Nampula
a5011.speech: Denounce the increase in crocodile attacks which have already caused dozens of fatalities, and ask for the construction of a bridge to facilitate the crossing of people and goods.

a5011.speaker: Population of Moma District, Nampula Province
a5011.name: Population of Moma District
a5011.title: Nampula Province
a5011.speech: Asks the Government to rehabilitate the road linking Mogovolas District to the main town of that coastal region; the traders whose businesses still survive say it is very complicated to continue with commercial activity because the journey of about two hundred kilometres can take more than ten hours.

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of the Republic of Ghana
a5108.speech: On Africa's role in the UN's founding: “At this 80th session of the United Nations General Assembly, I would like to speak about Africa’s role in the future of the organisation. However, it is impossible to do that without first considering the collective role that Africa played in its founding, which was small and relatively insignificant.” Of the 51 Member States involved in the founding of the United Nations in 1945, only four were African: Egypt, Ethiopia, Liberia, and South Africa; out of the 42 founding member states of the League of Nations, only three were African. “In the past, the majority of the 54 nations that now comprise Africa were never offered a seat at the table where plans for a new World Order were being drawn.”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On Africa's future: “As fate would have it, the tables have turned, and Africa’s role in the authorship of whatever is yet to come for this world will be huge, and it will be consequential... by the year 2050, more than 25% of the world’s population is expected to come from the African continent... So, you see, the future is African. Allow me to say this once again, a little louder for the people in the back. The future is African!” ; “Already today, Africa is a catalyst for human potential and development, as well as for economic reform and ecological stability. Africa is a catalyst for systemic change. If this reality—which is fact-based and straightforward—seems provocative or unsettling, perhaps it’s because you’re viewing it through the lens of centuries of racism, colonialism, imperialism, and the resulting implicit bias.”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On Ghana's economic reset: “Faced with rising inflation, a huge debt burden, and low morale amongst our citizens, my new administration quickly embarked on an ambitious programme of comprehensive transformation designed to restructure Ghana’s economic foundation and enhance our competitive standing globally. We refer to this process of recalibration as our reset agenda. In just eight months, we have achieved a significant reduction in inflation, from 23.8% in December 2024 to 11.5% in August 2025, restoring price stability for our citizens. Additionally, the Ghana cedi has appreciated considerably against other currencies, with Bloomberg reporting it as the best-performing currency in the world at one point... Our 24-Hour Economy Initiative promises to transform our economy.”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On UN reform and the Security Council: “I believe that, in honour of this milestone celebration, the United Nations should also embark on a process of serious recalibration and establish its own reset agenda.” ; “The UN founding charter is outdated when it comes to representation. The most powerful post-World War 2 nations are still being rewarded with an almost totalitarian guardianship over the rest of the world... If this were truly the case, a continent as large as Africa with its numerous UN Member states would have at least one permanent seat on the Security Council. Furthermore, veto power should not be restricted to five nations, nor should it be absolute. There must be a mechanism for the General Assembly to challenge a veto. No single nation should be able to exercise an absolute veto to serve its own interests in a conflict.” ; “Thirty years later, we African leaders are still making the same request: for a permanent seat on the Security Council, with the power of veto. So, today, Madam President, I stand here in this exact spot, asking: if not now, then when? We demand not only a reform of the Security Council, but also a reset of the global financial architecture, which is currently rigged against Africa. Africa must have a greater say in the world's multilateral financial institutions.”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On Cuba: “While I am making requests, I would like to call for the removal of the blockade on Cuba... The Cuban people shed their blood on African soil in the fight against apartheid. Indeed, Cuba has been, and continues to be, a faithful friend to Africa.”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On multilateralism, technology and disinformation: “In many ways, the United Nations is the proverbial town square of our modern global village. And it has never been more critical for us to protect this one space that brings and holds the world’s nations together as a community. The Internet, social media platforms, and Artificial Intelligence offer us the illusion of connectivity, when in fact they reinforce isolation by using algorithms that ensure we do not receive new ideas and perspectives, but rather more of the same. We are served alternative facts and manipulated images, making it easier to disseminate disinformation and sow seeds of division. These are dangerous times. Our world is currently experiencing a rise in nationalism and economic instability. There is a general breakdown of multilateralism...”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On Palestine and Gaza: “The denial of visas to President Abbas and the Palestinian delegation sets a bad precedent and should be deeply worrying to all member nations. Ghana recognised the state of Palestine in 1988 and supported a two-state solution to the conflict. Contrary to the claims of some, a two-state solution would not be a reward for Hamas but, rather, a reprieve for the hundreds of thousands of innocent people who have been facing collective punishment and forced starvation for no reason other than the fact that they are Palestinian... it doesn’t matter what you call it: if it looks like a duck, swims like a duck, and quacks like a duck, well then… It must be a duck. The crimes in Gaza must stop.”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On Sudan and migration: “I want to draw particular attention to the conflict in Sudan, which this body has described as the world’s largest humanitarian crisis. Twelve million people have had to flee their homes. When we speak of migration, we refer to the 12 million new refugees, whom we, as a global community, should be willing to assist in much the same way that many member nations readily assisted new refugees from Ukraine. Let’s dispense with euphemisms and dog-whistles and speak frankly. It’s not a mystery that when leaders of Western nations complain of their migration problems, they are often referring to immigrants from the Global South. Many of those migrants are climate refugees. Interestingly, the Global North emits 75% more greenhouse gases than the Global South. However, the effects of climate change are more severe in the Global South because we lack the resources to address them effectively.” ; “We cannot normalise cruelty. We cannot normalise hatred. We cannot normalise xenophobia and racism... These are not invaders or criminals.”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On reparations: “The slave trade must be recognised as the greatest crime against humanity. As African Champion on reparations, Ghana intends to introduce a motion in this August body to that effect. More than twelve and a half million Africans were forcibly taken against their will and transported to create wealth for the powerful Western nations. We must demand reparations for the enslavement of our people and the colonisation of our land that resulted in the theft of natural resources, as well as the looting of artefacts and other items of cultural heritage that have yet to be returned in total. We recognise the value of our land and the value of our lives.”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On aid cuts and resource sovereignty: “An increasingly insecure world is witnessing upward spending on defence budgets of bilateral partners and steep cuts in Official Development Assistance. Since July 2024, there has been a 40% drop in humanitarian aid to Africa. In this era of global uncertainty, Africa must exercise sovereignty over its natural resources to raise the necessary funds to ensure the well-being of its citizens.
