The days of parceling out vast concession areas to foreign interests for exploitation must come to an end. We will continue to welcome foreign investment, but we must negotiate better for a bigger share of the natural resources that belong to us. We are tired of the continued image of poverty-stricken, disease-ridden rural communities, living at the periphery of huge foreign-controlled natural resource concession areas. We are tired of having people extract the most they can from us and, in return, offer us the very least by way of respect, consideration, and dignity.”

a5108.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a5108.name: John Dramani Mahama
a5108.title: President of Ghana
a5108.speech: On women and representation: “I want to add that for the sake of Africa, and quite selfishly, for the sake of my 18-year-old daughter, I hope this new world that is arriving is a place of safety and equality for women and girls. To succeed, we must empower everyone, including women and girls, to reach their full potential.” ; “I would also like to congratulate Her Excellency Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang on being the first woman Vice President of Ghana. Now every Ghanaian girl knows the heights to which she can ascend. Words matter, but issues of representation matter even more, which is why Ghana looks forward to the appointment of a woman as Secretary General of this organisation in the future.”

a5108.speaker: Winston Churchill (quoted)
a5108.name: Winston Churchill (quoted)
a5108.speech: Declaring that “an iron curtain has descended across the Continent.”

a5108.speaker: UN Charter, Chapter 2, Article 1 (document)
a5108.name: UN Charter
a5108.title: Chapter 2, Article 1 (document)
a5108.speech: “The Organisation is based on the principle of the sovereign equality of all its members.”

a5108.speaker: Nelson Mandela (quoted, 1995 address to the UN)
a5108.name: Nelson Mandela (quoted
a5108.title: 1995 address to the UN)
a5108.speech: “The United Nations has to reassess its role, redefine its profile, and reshape its structures. It should truly reflect the diversity of our universe and ensure equity among the nations in the exercise of power within the system of international relations. In general, and the Security Council in particular.”

a5108.speaker: Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's founder (quoted)
a5108.name: Kwame Nkrumah
a5108.title: Ghana's founder (quoted)
a5108.speech: “We seek to be friends of all and enemies to none.”

a5108.speaker: Warsan Shire, Somali-British poet (quoted, poem “Home”)
a5108.name: Warsan Shire
a5108.title: Somali-British poet (quoted, poem “Home”)
a5108.speech: “You have to understand / that no one puts their children in a boat / unless the water is safer than the land / No one burns their palms / under trains / beneath carriages / No one spends days and nights in the stomach of a truck / feeding on newspaper unless the miles travelled / means something more than journey.”

a5108.speaker: Arundhati Roy, Indian-American writer (quoted)
a5108.name: Arundhati Roy
a5108.title: Indian-American writer (quoted)
a5108.speech: “Another world is not only possible, she is on her way. On a quiet day, I can hear her breathing.”

a5249.speaker: Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, Governor of Adamawa State, represented by Bello Hamman Diram, Commissioner for Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Humanitarian Services
a5249.name: Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri
a5249.title: Governor of Adamawa State, represented by Bello Hamman Diram, Commissioner for Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Humanitarian Services
a5249.speech: Expressed profound gratitude to KSrelief for its generous support, emphasizing that the assistance comes at a crucial time, reinforcing his administration's broader recovery and development agenda: "This humanitarian gesture strengthens the bond of friendship between our nations and exemplifies the shared values of compassion, solidarity, and humanity" ; reaffirmed the state's commitment to sustainable solutions for IDPs, highlighting the State Action Plan, which outlines a strategic framework encompassing shelter, healthcare, education, livelihood empowerment, and logistics.

a5249.speaker: Zubaida Umar, NEMA Director-General, represented by Onibode A. Bandele, Director of Planning, Research and Forecasting
a5249.name: Zubaida Umar
a5249.title: NEMA Director-General, represented by Onibode A. Bandele, Director of Planning, Research and Forecasting
a5249.speech: Commended the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for its unwavering commitment to humanitarian assistance in Nigeria, emphasizing that the intervention aligns with the shared vision of both nations to promote "Unrestricted Humanity"-ensuring lifesaving aid reaches those in dire need.

a5362.speaker: Wilmot Paye, Liberian Minister of Mines and Energy
a5362.name: Wilmot Paye
a5362.title: Liberian Minister of Mines and Energy
a5362.speech: Has predicted a new future for Liberia’s development agenda, stating that the mining sector presents a perfect opportunity for growth; indicated that findings of the survey would propel the country for new heights and possibilities for future development. “This should present us an opportunity for growth” ; “This is a significant step to boost the sector.”

a5362.speaker: Wilmot Paye, Liberian Minister of Mines and Energy
a5362.name: Wilmot Paye
a5362.title: Liberian Minister of Mines and Energy
a5362.speech: Noted that the handover is a testament of the elevation of China-Liberia ties by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai: “China has proven to be one of Liberia’s partners. It was our pledge to get Liberia’s geological information”, and also lauded other partners including the United Kingdom, United States for their support over the years; according to him, the survey will serve as a useful guide the country in setting aside protected areas.

a5362.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a5362.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a5362.title: Vice President of Liberia
a5362.speech: Underscored the mineral sector’s pivotal role in Liberia’s economy; stressed that the sector not only contributes significantly to the nation’s GDP but is also the backbone of Liberia’s exports. “With mineral resources contributing an impressive 52 percent to Liberia’s GDP and accounting for 93 percent of its exports, we must harness this potential for sustainable development” ; “This is a monumental step for Liberia” ; “Our nation’s mineral wealth, if managed effectively, has the potential to transform Liberia and lift countless people out of poverty” ; emphasized that responsible exploration and extraction could maximize returns, providing jobs and infrastructure development.

a5362.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a5362.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a5362.title: Vice President of Liberia
a5362.speech: Expressed the government’s gratitude to the People’s Republic of China for its continued support and collaboration; acknowledged China’s contribution as a testament to Liberia’s expanding partnerships and growing influence in the global mining industry; also acknowledged the historical contributions of the United States and the United Kingdom in advancing Liberia’s mining sector, reminding attendees that these partnerships have paved the way for Liberia’s current progress and that international allies have long recognized the nation’s potential. “We remember those who have helped us, and we hope to build on those foundations.”

a5362.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a5362.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a5362.title: Vice President of Liberia
a5362.speech: Noted that previous studies were either incomplete or outdated, underscoring the importance of up-to-date data for investors and policymakers: “For Liberia to thrive, we need current information that reflects our real potential” ; emphasized that the survey would lay the foundation for a more stable economy, with the data able to attract foreign investment and lead to a more regulated mining industry.

a5362.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a5362.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a5362.title: Vice President of Liberia
a5362.speech: Extended an invitation to local and international investors, arguing that the clarity provided by this new data could attract investors looking for new opportunities: “Liberia is open for business, and we have the resources to back it up.”

a5362.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a5362.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a5362.title: Vice President of Liberia
a5362.speech: Acknowledged the environmental impact of mining and promised that the government would take steps to ensure sustainable practices; called for responsible mining to protect Liberia’s rich biodiversity; mentioned that the survey data would also help create more environmentally conscious policies.

a5362.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a5362.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a5362.title: Vice President of Liberia
a5362.speech: Promised that the survey results would be used to bring more transparency to the mining sector, with clear guidelines and regulations: “We want to ensure that the wealth from our resources benefits the people of Liberia, not just a few” ; asserted that local communities should be the primary beneficiaries of mining activities, and that Liberia should capitalize on its resources to foster economic independence and reduce reliance on foreign aid.

a5362.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a5362.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a5362.title: Vice President of Liberia
a5362.speech: Called on Liberians to support the government’s efforts to develop the mining sector, reminding citizens that responsible management of mineral resources is essential for Liberia’s progress: “Together, we can make our mineral wealth a blessing for all.”

a5543.speaker: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou, Beninese magistrate in exile in the United States (open letter)
a5543.name: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou
a5543.title: Beninese magistrate in exile in the United States (open letter)
a5543.speech: Says he took up his pen with a heavy heart to claim his inalienable right to speak and to denounce the continual harassment to which he is subjected by the authorities of his country; states that because of the rulings he handed down in the notorious cases of attempted poisoning of the Head of State and of undermining state security, he is persecuted and his exile has not stopped his pursuers in their base design to kill him, if not physically, then at least socially and professionally.

a5543.speaker: Beninese government communiqué of Thursday 22 May 2014 (broadcast on national television)
a5543.name: Beninese government communiqué of Thursday 22 May 2014 (broadcast on national television)
a5543.speech: Invited Judge Houssou to resume service by 26 May 2014 at the latest, failing which he would be considered to have resigned.

a5543.speaker: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou, Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.name: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou
a5543.title: Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.speech: Denounces what he calls the machiavellianism of the authors of the communiqué, saying it is manifestly insincere and therefore a “non-lieu” (no case to answer), because it is impossible for him to resume service on 26 May 2014 for two fundamental reasons: the conditions of his security are still not clearly met in the country, as a price remains on his head from those who felt wronged by his two dismissal orders; and he is engaged in an asylum procedure in the United States. He adds that the authors of the communiqué are wrong to treat his exile as a fiction and to call him back as if he had gone on a pleasure trip, saying he left Benin in the face of the complicit negligence of the competent authorities in protecting him against arbitrariness and the base instincts of a losing and frantic vengeance.

a5543.speaker: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou, Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.name: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou
a5543.title: Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.speech: Says he is not against forgiveness, but raises questions about the presidential pardon: what does this pardon conceal, how sincere is it, is it the best thing to do in a drama that has so divided the people and broken whole lives, why does it come at the precise moment when the Supreme Court has handed down its rulings, what is to be said of a pardon granted when it was not requested, and of a pardon intended for people who benefited from a dismissal of charges. He declares that he does not ask to be pardoned because he has done nothing to justify it, that he is not detained in the case but forced into exile as a perfect victim, and that “one does not forgive a victim; one asks a victim for forgiveness, apologises to them and restores them in their inalienable right to live in peace and security in their homeland.” He concludes that it is easy to forgive when one has finished taking revenge.

a5543.speaker: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou, Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.name: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou
a5543.title: Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.speech: Describes the persecution he endured: he was called “corrupt judge”, “steeped in charlatanism”, “leading a loose life”; crowds marched against him across the country threatening mob justice; his head was demanded in places of worship; journalists were set loose to sully his name; friends and relatives were infiltrated to spy on him. He notes with one consolation that none of his accusers managed to provide proof of their lying allegations and that his decisions were never contradicted, at least legally. He recounts crossing bush, mud and river to flee Benin and arriving in the United States on 1 December 2013, where he was detained for eighteen days over a visa problem before the credibility of his fear was recognised, and thanks the US authorities.

a5543.speaker: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou, Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.name: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou
a5543.title: Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.speech: States that in law the facts brought before him did not constitute offences under criminal law; that since 17 May 2013 when he said so in his orders, no other judge has proved the contrary and no serious jurist has taken the opposite view; that his decisions were confirmed on appeal; that the Supreme Court did not rule on his orders but quashed the confirmatory rulings of the indictment chamber on a point of form, over a simple visa problem; and that the decision of the differently composed indictment chamber of Monday 19 May 2014 releasing the accused on provisional liberty is merely a partial execution of his dismissal orders of 17 May 2013.

a5543.speaker: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou, Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.name: Judge Angelo Djidjoho Houssou
a5543.title: Beninese magistrate in exile (open letter)
a5543.speech: Commits to a more active citizenship based on the exercise of his right to speak and his duty to contribute to improving his country’s governance; says the contemporary judge must avoid isolating himself and be accessible to the public and interested in the life of his city; warns that as long as politics remains the preserve of people whose tendency to failure is matched only by their greed, the country cannot emerge from underdevelopment; says his country seems handed over to people without faith or law, that its leaders have renounced their duty to build a society of values, order, justice and security, and that the drama of his country is not so much these venomous practices as the silence of enlightened consciences and the compromise of elites; and declares that he is no longer afraid of anything, not even death, and that Benin can count on him to play his part fully — “we will not let it perish in just any hands!”

a5543.speaker: William Arthur Ward (quoted)
a5543.name: William Arthur Ward (quoted)
a5543.speech: Forgiveness “warms the heart and cools the sting.”

a5543.speaker: François Verillon (quoted)
a5543.name: François Verillon (quoted)
a5543.speech: Forgiveness is “neither a wipe of the sponge nor a wash, but a re-creation.”

a5543.speaker: Josh Billings (quoted)
a5543.name: Josh Billings (quoted)
a5543.speech: “There is no revenge so complete as forgiveness.”

a5543.speaker: Arab proverb (quoted)
a5543.name: Arab proverb (quoted)
a5543.speech: Forgiveness is “the most beautiful flower of victory.”

a5629.speaker: Dr Busola Tejumola, MultiChoice Executive Head, General Entertainment Channels
a5629.name: Dr Busola Tejumola
a5629.title: MultiChoice Executive Head, General Entertainment Channels
a5629.speech: Assesses the impact of television as the world marks World Television Day, saying television — both its content and its technology — has become the backbone of African culture.

a5629.speaker: Somalia's Ministry of Ports and Marine Transports (official Notice)
a5629.name: Somalia's Ministry of Ports and Marine Transports (official Notice)
a5629.speech: Has imposed a mandatory Electronic Cargo Tracking Number (ECTN) requirement for all Somali ports, according to an official Notice from the Ministry obtained by Horn Observer.

a5629.speaker: Mohamed Ali, Head of Trade and Commercial Attaché at the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a5629.name: Mohamed Ali
a5629.title: Head of Trade and Commercial Attaché at the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a5629.speech: Speaking at the recently held Embassies Business Fair and Conference, emphasized the pivotal role of Somalia and South Africa in unlocking new horizons in trade and economic diplomacy.

a5629.speaker: Somali Stock Exchange (SSE)
a5629.name: Somali Stock Exchange (SSE)
a5629.speech: Has announced the launch of the Somali Capital Markets Forum, scheduled to take place on 23 June 2025 in Mogadishu.

a5707.speaker: Cristian Signoretto, Eni’s director for global gas and LNG portfolio
a5707.name: Cristian Signoretto
a5707.title: Eni’s director for global gas and LNG portfolio
a5707.speech: told reporters on the sidelines of a conference on Sunday that Eni is in talks with Japan on supplying the country with liquefied natural gas ; “We already deal with Japanese buyers on a short-term basis and we would like to expand that collaboration also to a long-term basis,” adding that Eni plans to bring more LNG volumes to the market, including from Indonesia and also wants Japanese financial institutions to support some projects; he added that Eni plans to build its LNG portfolio to 18 million metric tonnes per year by 2027 and would be ready to commit part of it to Japan, if the opportunity is there.

a5707.speaker: Cristian Signoretto, Eni’s director for global gas and LNG portfolio
a5707.name: Cristian Signoretto
a5707.title: Eni’s director for global gas and LNG portfolio
a5707.speech: said it was early to say about the specifics of the discussions, including whether Eni would insist on destination clauses ; “Flexibility will be part of the discussion,” Signoretto said, without providing details.

a5852.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Minister of Health
a5852.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a5852.title: Namibian Minister of Health
a5852.speech: Welcomed the decision by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to approve a "humanitarian exemption" ensuring that millions of people worldwide, including in Namibia, continue to receive life-saving HIV treatment; warned that a withdrawal of American support could have devastating consequences: "That should not happen at all. Matters that concern human lives must always be preserved" ; suspects the original decision may not have been sufficiently thought through and is now being corrected.

a5852.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Minister of Health
a5852.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a5852.title: Namibian Minister of Health
a5852.speech: Stressed that important health programmes will be continued even if US support ceases permanently, and assured the public that Namibia's health programmes are secure even in the event of a complete withdrawal of US aid: "All our programmes are an integral part of the ministry's core activities" ; said the government has budgeted annually for operating and capital costs since independence and that international donations are valuable but merely supplementary.

a5852.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS Executive Director
a5852.name: Winnie Byanyima
a5852.title: UNAIDS Executive Director
a5852.speech: "UNAIDS welcomes this important decision by the US government, which guarantees millions of people access to life-saving HIV medicines during the review of foreign aid."

a5852.speaker: Namibian Ministry of Health
a5852.name: Namibian Ministry of Health
a5852.speech: According to the Health Ministry, essential programmes are not at risk.

a5852.speaker: US State Department (announcement)
a5852.name: US State Department (announcement)
a5852.speech: Signalled a temporary suspension of foreign aid programmes - including those under PEPFAR - while Donald Trump reassesses international development assistance.

a5852.speaker: US suspension order to USAID in Zimbabwe (official instruction)
a5852.name: US suspension order to USAID in Zimbabwe (official instruction)
a5852.speech: USAID in Zimbabwe was instructed to halt all activities under a specific agreement, including projects on diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility (DEIA); organisations must demonstrate that DEIA activities have been suspended, minimise their costs, review their contracts and submit detailed reports on how DEIA-related work can be discontinued while ensuring compliance with the suspension order.

a5852.speaker: Selma Shiwaya, spokeswoman for IntraHealth Namibia
a5852.name: Selma Shiwaya
a5852.title: spokeswoman for IntraHealth Namibia
a5852.speech: Stated that she could not comment on the possible effects of this decision on their operations.

a5853.speaker: Van Vranken, US Ambassador to Botswana
a5853.name: Van Vranken
a5853.title: US Ambassador to Botswana
a5853.speech: Said in his opening remarks at the US Africa Command (AFRICOM) African Chiefs of Defense Conference 2024 in Gaborone that Botswana is "a steadfast partner of the United States."

a5853.speaker: Van Vranken, US Ambassador to Botswana
a5853.name: Van Vranken
a5853.title: US Ambassador to Botswana
a5853.speech: Announced to the Conference that Botswana will soon host AFRICOM's flagship military exercise, Southern Accord 2024.

a5853.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, head of Niger's ruling Conseil National pour la sauvegarde de la patrie (CNSP)
a5853.name: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani
a5853.title: head of Niger's ruling Conseil National pour la sauvegarde de la patrie (CNSP)
a5853.speech: Has given the US up to September 15th, 2024 to have completed withdrawal of troops.

a5853.speaker: Niger and Chad (governments)
a5853.name: Niger and Chad (governments)
a5853.speech: Have already called for withdrawal of US troops.

a5864.speaker: Niassa Provincial Executive Council (note / provincial authorities)
a5864.name: Niassa Provincial Executive Council (note / provincial authorities)
a5864.speech: Announced that the Irish government plans to invest 406.8 million meticais (EUR5.4 million) in social infrastructure projects in Niassa province ; according to the note, the funding, which will be implemented up until 2030, will contribute to the construction of boarding schools, solar-powered water supply systems, a maternal and child health unit, as well as irrigation and processing systems "to improve the agricultural value chain", among others.

a5864.speaker: Edgar Ussene, representative of the Irish Embassy in Niassa
a5864.name: Edgar Ussene
a5864.title: representative of the Irish Embassy in Niassa
a5864.speech: "Our partnership goes beyond financing; it is about contributing to the promotion of sustainable development and the construction of a dignified future."

a5864.speaker: Celestina Teofilo, director of the provincial governor's office
a5864.name: Celestina Teofilo
a5864.title: director of the provincial governor's office
a5864.speech: Said Irish funding places the population at the centre of priorities, "guaranteeing sustainable results" for the province's development.

a6038.speaker: Bénin Web TV
a6038.name: Bénin Web TV
a6038.speech: Reports a "slight rise in prices in January 2025" in the country, specifying that the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) reached 100.7 in January 2025 against 100.4 in December 2024, an increase of 0.3%, mainly attributed to the rise in the prices of food products and transport.

a6038.speaker: Financial Afrik
a6038.name: Financial Afrik
a6038.speech: Points out that Tidjane Thiam is facing a situation of "Ivoirité", wondering whether a scenario similar to that of Barack Obama could occur in Africa; although his investiture as the PDCI-RDA candidate seemed assured for the October 2025 presidential election, he suddenly finds himself under fire from critics, including within his own camp.

a6038.speaker: Jeune Afrique
a6038.name: Jeune Afrique
a6038.speech: Reports that former president Laurent Gbagbo is engaged in a "perpetual struggle", seeming to have a "taste of the unfinished"; at 80 years old, the former president has begun a new fight — his re-registration on the Ivorian electoral rolls with a view to standing in the presidential election — and recently launched a mobilisation tour.

a6038.speaker: Abidjan.net
a6038.name: Abidjan.net
a6038.speech: Reports that the 15th edition of the Forum of the Trade Union New Year of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC)-Africa opened on Tuesday 25 February 2025 at Grand-Bassam under the chairmanship of Robert Beugré Mambé.

a6038.speaker: Robert Beugré Mambé, Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire, Minister of Sports and of the Living Environment
a6038.name: Robert Beugré Mambé
a6038.title: Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire, Minister of Sports and of the Living Environment
a6038.speech: Praised the trade unionists' spirit of social dialogue; in his address, the head of government encouraged trade unionists to continue their engagement in constructive social dialogue, a guarantee of economic and social progress.

a6038.speaker: Le Monde Afrique
a6038.name: Le Monde Afrique
a6038.speech: Highlights the Senegalese government's difficulties in managing the public accounts, indicating that the country's debt has reached 99.67% of GDP and the budget deficit 12.3%, according to the Court of Auditors.

a6038.speaker: Court of Auditors of Senegal (Cour des comptes)
a6038.name: Court of Auditors of Senegal (Cour des comptes)
a6038.speech: The country's debt reaches 99.67% of GDP and the budget deficit 12.3%, according to the Court of Auditors.

a6038.speaker: Government of Senegal
a6038.name: Government of Senegal
a6038.speech: Assures that it will not resort to a course of austerity.

a6038.speaker: Walf Quotidien
a6038.name: Walf Quotidien
a6038.speech: Reports that the construction and public works sector is "under tension", confronted with domestic debt, bank claims, tax problems and difficult cash flow; adds that the situation appears worrying for the agri-food industries because of the second announced reduction in the prices of basic necessities ; concerning the suspension of the American government aid agency (USAID), notes that former president Macky Sall "plays down the measure" taken by Donald Trump.

a6038.speaker: Macky Sall, former President of Senegal (in L'AS)
a6038.name: Macky Sall
a6038.title: former President of Senegal (in L'AS)
a6038.speech: "Africa is no longer in a perspective of holding out its hand."

a6096.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6096.name: Donald Trump
a6096.title: US President
a6096.speech: has called for the chair of the Federal Reserve to quit right away. "'Too Late' should resign immediately!!!", Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. He also included a link to a news article about a US federal housing regulator calling for Mr Powell to be investigated over his testimony about renovations to the central bank's Washington headquarters.

a6096.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6096.name: Donald Trump
a6096.title: US President
a6096.speech: he said earlier this year that had "no intention of firing him" [Powell].

a6096.speaker: Jerome Powell, chair of the US Federal Reserve
a6096.name: Jerome Powell
a6096.title: chair of the US Federal Reserve
a6096.speech: said on Tuesday that the Fed would have cut rates already had it not been for the impact of Trump's tariff policies. When asked during a meeting of central bankers in Portugal whether US rates would have been cut again this year if the administration had not announced its plan to sharply increase tariffs on countries around the world Mr Powell responded, "I think that's right."

a6096.speaker: Jerome Powell, chair of the US Federal Reserve
a6096.name: Jerome Powell
a6096.title: chair of the US Federal Reserve
a6096.speech: Ahead of Trump's return to power at the start of this year, Mr Powell said he would not step down if the president asked him to and that it is "not permitted under law" for the White House to force him out.

a6096.speaker: Jerome Powell, chair of the US Federal Reserve
a6096.name: Jerome Powell
a6096.title: chair of the US Federal Reserve
a6096.speech: Last week, Mr Powell told the Senate that reports about soaring costs and expensive features at the Fed's headquarters were "misleading and inaccurate in many, many respects."

a6096.speaker: US Federal Reserve
a6096.name: US Federal Reserve
a6096.speech: declined to comment about Trump's remarks when contacted by the BBC.

a6096.speaker: Bill Pulte, Federal Housing Finance Agency director
a6096.name: Bill Pulte
a6096.title: Federal Housing Finance Agency director
a6096.speech: called for Mr Powell to be investigated. "I am asking Congress to investigate Chairman Jerome Powell, his political bias, and his deceptive Senate testimony, which is enough to be removed 'for cause'," he posted on X.

a6096.speaker: US Supreme Court, landmark 1935 ruling
a6096.name: US Supreme Court
a6096.title: landmark 1935 ruling
a6096.speech: Board members of independent federal agencies like the Federal Reserve can only be forced out before their terms expire "for cause," according to a landmark US Supreme Court ruling in 1935.

a6135.speaker: Ukrainian Ministry of Infrastructure
a6135.name: Ukrainian Ministry of Infrastructure
a6135.speech: Announced that a humanitarian vessel chartered by the UN had left the port of Pivdenny with 23,000 tonnes of wheat on board: “The vessel Brave Commander with grain for Africa has left the port of Pivdenny. This morning, the cargo ship departed for the port of Djibouti, where the food will be delivered on arrival to consumers in Ethiopia” (on Telegram).

a6135.speaker: Marine Traffic
a6135.name: Marine Traffic
a6135.speech: According to information transmitted by Marine Traffic, the arrival of this first shipment in Djibouti is expected on 25 August.

a6135.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6135.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6135.speech: Declared that the shipment is “an important step for the reintegration of Ukrainian food production into the global food market and makes it possible to assist countries hit by major food shortages via commercial and humanitarian corridors.”

a6135.speaker: Oleksandr Kubrakov, Ukrainian Infrastructure Minister
a6135.name: Oleksandr Kubrakov
a6135.title: Ukrainian Infrastructure Minister
a6135.speech: Had said he hoped that “two or three” additional vessels chartered by the UN could leave from the port of Pivdenny soon.

a6135.speaker: US Agency for International Development (USAID) (press statement)
a6135.name: US Agency for International Development (USAID) (press statement)
a6135.speech: Specified in a statement on Tuesday that it had provided 68 million dollars to the UN World Food Programme (WFP) for the purchase, transport and storage of 150,000 tonnes of Ukrainian wheat ; “USAID […] supported the first humanitarian shipment of grain to leave the Black Sea via the Ukrainian port of Yuzhny today,” the statement indicates, specifying that before the war Ukraine was one of the WFP's main suppliers of grain.

a6135.speaker: United Nations
a6135.name: United Nations
a6135.speech: According to the United Nations, between 1 and 15 August, 11 bulk carriers were authorised to leave Odesa, 6 Chornomorsk and 4 Pivdenny; these 21 vessels carried in total 563,317 tonnes of agricultural raw materials, including 451,481 tonnes of maize, the main recipients being Turkey (26% of volumes), Iran (22%) and South Korea (22%).

a6186.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB) (press release)
a6186.name: African Development Bank (AfDB) (press release)
a6186.speech: According to an AfDB press release, access to an efficient and cost-effective long-distance bulk transport service thanks to the single electrified standard-gauge track will encourage large-scale mining and commercial agriculture; according to the same press release, this railway will transform the central transport corridor into an economic corridor by improving commercial and manufacturing opportunities along the corridor's area of influence.

a6289.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6289.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6289.speech: Welcomed on Friday an exceptional donation for refugees of 23,268 tonnes of rice offered by the South Korean Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA), the largest South Korean contribution since it began supporting refugees in Kenya in 2018 ; WFP has been forced to cut rations to one third of the normal quantity for lack of funding despite the support of several partners.

a6289.speaker: Baimankay Sankoh, WFP Deputy Country Director
a6289.name: Baimankay Sankoh
a6289.title: WFP Deputy Country Director
a6289.speech: “This generous contribution is vital as the number of refugees in Kenya continues to grow” ; “The majority depend entirely on humanitarian aid. This support comes at just the right time.”

a6289.speaker: Kang Hyung-shik, Ambassador of South Korea to Kenya
a6289.name: Kang Hyung-shik
a6289.title: Ambassador of South Korea to Kenya
a6289.speech: “The Republic of Korea is proud to contribute to alleviating the hunger crisis in the region” ; “Our humanitarian commitment rests on a tradition of international solidarity.”

a6291.speaker: Dr. Dele Alake, Minister of Solid Minerals Development and Chairman of the African Minerals Strategy Group (AMSG)
a6291.name: Dr. Dele Alake
a6291.title: Minister of Solid Minerals Development and Chairman of the African Minerals Strategy Group (AMSG)
a6291.speech: Has called for a bold new vision to make minerals the fulcrum of Africa's transformative industrialization. “Africa's minerals have powered industrialization elsewhere while our own economies remain under-industrialized. This paradox must end. Our vision must be clear: to move from extractive dependence to transformative industrialization,” Dr. Alake declared in a statement issued on Sunday, October 5, 2025, in Abuja ; delivering the keynote address at African Mining Week in Cape Town, the minister emphasized that Africa must no longer be content as a supplier of raw minerals but must become a global hub for mineral processing, innovation, and green industrialization, and noted that the continent is blessed with some of the world's richest mineral deposits, key to clean energy, digital technologies, advanced manufacturing, and global security ; “Our youth should no longer seek jobs abroad while opportunities lie buried beneath their feet. The time to industrialize is now. Let us set the stage for an Africa that is not just a participant in the global minerals economy, but a driver of its future,” Alake asserted.

a6291.speaker: Dr. Dele Alake, Minister of Solid Minerals Development (represented by Permanent Secretary Dr. Farouk Yabo)
a6291.name: Dr. Dele Alake
a6291.title: Minister of Solid Minerals Development (represented by Permanent Secretary Dr. Farouk Yabo)
a6291.speech: Highlighting Nigeria's ongoing reforms in the mining sector, said the nation is incentivizing local beneficiation from gold refining to lithium processing, revoking dormant licenses to encourage serious investment, and strengthening transparency to attract credible global partners; added that Nigeria is also developing a National Critical Minerals Strategy and investing in digital systems for data accessibility and mineral traceability ; reiterated Nigeria's commitment to creating a $1 trillion economy by 2030 through solid minerals development: “We are investing in digitizing mining processes from data accessibility to mineral traceability. We are also focusing on bequeathing strong institutions and the right policies to drive reforms. Hence, the ongoing efforts to amend the 2007 Minerals and Mining Act to provide a more robust legislative framework that will propel investments in the mining sector” ; emphasized that Nigeria's minerals will henceforth be traceable, originating only from licensed operators or formalized artisanal and small-scale miners.

a6291.speaker: Dr. Dele Alake, Minister of Solid Minerals Development and Chairman of AMSG
a6291.name: Dr. Dele Alake
a6291.title: Minister of Solid Minerals Development and Chairman of AMSG
a6291.speech: Urged African nations to prioritize mapping their mineral resources to understand their true potential. “After national mapping, it is the duty of countries to ensure only licensed operators are mining. We must also build adequate capacity for effective supervision,” he said.

a6291.speaker: Dr. Farouk Yabo, Permanent Secretary, Nigeria's Ministry of Solid Minerals Development
a6291.name: Dr. Farouk Yabo
a6291.title: Permanent Secretary, Nigeria's Ministry of Solid Minerals Development
a6291.speech: During the Country Spotlight Session, presented investment opportunities in the solid minerals sector, showcasing reforms, incentives, and a synopsis of the nation's mineral endowments.

a6311.speaker: Michael Usi, Malawi State Vice President
a6311.name: Michael Usi
a6311.title: Malawi State Vice President
a6311.speech: Has hailed the United States Agency for International Development (USaid)-funded five year Titukulane Project, describing it as a landmark initiative that has resulted in the sprouting of resilient communities across Malawi ; said the project had demonstrated that when stakeholders join hands, they can move mountains ; "The name Titukulane, meaning 'let's develop together', is a fitting testament to what this initiative has stood for; [that is], a hallmark of collaboration, resilience and shared purpose. Today, we celebrate not just the closeout of a five-year journey but the legacy of resilience, hope and self-actualisation. This is what Titukulane Project is leaving behind for the communities of Zomba, Mangochi and beyond."

a6311.speaker: Michael Usi, Malawi State Vice President
a6311.name: Michael Usi
a6311.title: Malawi State Vice President
a6311.speech: Said the project was the first of its kind, adding that it was designed around the National Resilience Strategy (NRS of 2018 to 2030)—coordinated through the Department of Disaster Management Affairs—which aimed to shift from a reactive cycle of disaster response to a proactive approach of risk management, preparedness and resilience building: "This shift is no small feat. For years, Malawi has been at the mercy of climate shocks, from floods and droughts to devastating cyclones that have exacerbated hunger across the country. Yet, with initiatives like the Titukulane Project, we are proving that vulnerability is not our destiny. By embedding climate-smart agricultural practices, diverse livelihood packages, community-driven disaster risk management and inclusive governance mechanisms, the project has shown us that resilience is achievable and sustainable."

a6311.speaker: Michael Usi, Malawi State Vice President
a6311.name: Michael Usi
a6311.title: Malawi State Vice President
a6311.speech: Said he was elated that the project had empowered community members not only to recover from shocks but to build stronger systems to withstand future ones: "I am greatly impressed with the figures from the project, impacting a total of 613,826 individuals with interventions in agriculture, irrigation, livestock, marketing, youth vocational skills development, Wash [water, sanitation and hygiene] and nutrition, including improving coordination of NRS interventions at national and district levels. Malawi can only develop if investments are channeled into building resilient systems."

a6311.speaker: Michael Usi, Malawi State Vice President
a6311.name: Michael Usi
a6311.title: Malawi State Vice President
a6311.speech: Hailed the project's alignment with the Malawi (MW) 2063 vision, saying this was another milestone worth celebrating: "Under MW2063, we envision an inclusive, self-reliant and industrialised middle-income nation. The Titukulane Project has contributed meaningfully to two pillars of this vision."

a6311.speaker: Pamela Kuwali, Country Director of Care Malawi
a6311.name: Pamela Kuwali
a6311.title: Country Director of Care Malawi
a6311.speech: Also hailed the project's successes: "The Titukulane Project has exemplified the power of collaboration, focusing on three key areas: increasing diversified incomes, improving nutritional status and enhancing institutional capacities. This approach has ensured women are at the forefront of our efforts. Notable achievements included empowering communities economically through village savings and loans associations."

a6311.speaker: Jones Chimpukuso, Chief of Party for Titukulane Resilience Food Security Activity
a6311.name: Jones Chimpukuso
a6311.title: Chief of Party for Titukulane Resilience Food Security Activity
a6311.speech: Said despite registering successes, there were challenges including the slow start of the project due to the Covid pandemic in 2020-21: "Major hurdles included tropical cyclones Gombe and Tropical Freddy, cholera, and, most recently, El Niño."

a6450.speaker: Reports on donor fund management (unspecified, cited)
a6450.name: Reports on donor fund management (unspecified
a6450.title: cited)
a6450.speech: Reports continue to highlight weak accountability frameworks, fund leakages, and delays in programme implementation.

a6450.speaker: Philip Agbese (APC, Benue), deputy spokesperson of the House of Representatives
a6450.name: Philip Agbese (APC
a6450.title: Benue), deputy spokesperson of the House of Representatives
a6450.speech: Noted that Nigeria received an estimated $1.8 billion from the Global Fund between 2021 and 2025 to fight HIV, tuberculosis (TB), and malaria, in addition to $2.8 billion in health assistance from USAID covering various health threats such as HIV, malaria, polio, and tuberculosis between 2022 and 2024 ; added that the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria, established in 2002, was created to accelerate global efforts to end these epidemics, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, through pooled financing and partnerships ; “Nigeria also received over $6 billion dollars in health assistance from the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief from 2021 to 2025 to fight HIV/AIDS and build capacity of Health and community Systems.”

a6450.speaker: Philip Agbese (APC, Benue), deputy spokesperson of the House of Representatives
a6450.name: Philip Agbese (APC
a6450.title: Benue), deputy spokesperson of the House of Representatives
a6450.speech: Expressed concern that despite these significant interventions, Nigeria continues to bear one of the highest global burdens of HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria, citing data that in 2023 alone about 15,000 children (aged 0–14 years) died from AIDS-related causes in Nigeria while 51,000 AIDS-related deaths were recorded nationwide, placing Nigeria third globally in HIV deaths and with the highest number of HIV cases in West and Central Africa; that Nigeria ranks first in Africa and sixth in the world in tuberculosis, accounting for 4.6 per cent of the global TB burden; and that in malaria the country bears the highest burden worldwide, representing 26.6 per cent of global cases and 31 per cent of global malaria deaths.

a6450.speaker: Philip Agbese (APC, Benue), deputy spokesperson of the House of Representatives
a6450.name: Philip Agbese (APC
a6450.title: Benue), deputy spokesperson of the House of Representatives
a6450.speech: Expressed worry that the alarming statistics raise questions about the transparency, coordination, and impact of the grants, especially given that the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare is responsible for implementing USAID-funded projects while the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) Nigeria oversees Global Fund programmes ; lamented that there has not been a coordinated and robust oversight by the National Assembly on the utilisation of these grants, despite its constitutional powers under Sections 88 and 89 of the Constitution ; warned that unless urgent steps are taken to reevaluate and reassess how the grants have been implemented, especially as the Global Fund prepares its 8th Replenishment phase, Nigeria risks failing to meet the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) target of eliminating HIV, TB, and malaria by 2030.

a6450.speaker: House of Representatives (resolution)
a6450.name: House of Representatives (resolution)
a6450.speech: Resolved to investigate the utilisation of over $4.6 billion in health grants and assistance received by Nigeria from the Global Fund and USAID between 2021 and 2025; mandated its Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control to investigate the utilisation of the grants and report back within four weeks; and resolved to mandate the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare to provide details of the implementation plan and National Assembly approvals for the utilisation and expenditure of the grants.

a6492.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a6492.name: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a6492.speech: Expressed deep concern at the simultaneous deterioration of the health and food situation in Sudan, a country gripped by civil war for more than two years ; estimates that it needs 120 million dollars to scale up its humanitarian aid in Tawila over the next three months, funding considered essential to contain the epidemic and maintain basic services.

a6492.speaker: Farhan Haq, deputy spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General
a6492.name: Farhan Haq
a6492.title: deputy spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General
a6492.speech: According to him, “nearly 60% of displaced families still do not have adequate shelter” despite the humanitarian aid provided by the UN and its partners.

a6492.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) system
a6492.name: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) system
a6492.speech: Has identified famine conditions in several areas of North Darfur and the eastern Nuba Mountains, warning that the situation is expected to worsen further during the lean season, from July to October, in conflict zones where humanitarian access remains limited.

a6522.speaker: The United States and its western allies
a6522.name: The United States and its western allies
a6522.speech: Announced support for Israel and pledged further weapons and military assistance to Israel.

a6522.speaker: Kaire Mbuende, Ambassador
a6522.name: Kaire Mbuende
a6522.title: Ambassador
a6522.speech: Spoke to nbc's News Anchor, Elago Shitaatala, to give background on the long-running conflict.

a6622.speaker: Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Health Minister
a6622.name: Kalumbi Shangula
a6622.title: Namibian Health Minister
a6622.speech: Emphasized that this year's theme highlights the importance of safeguarding human rights to ensure integrated and affordable access to health services and social protection for everyone by 2030. ; "Anyone can encounter mental health challenges at some point. Studies have shown that people living with HIV are twice as likely to face mental health issues like depression, anxiety, and harmful substance use, which can hinder their ability to seek care or adhere to treatment. The Global AIDS Strategy 2021-2026 identifies the integration of mental health and psychosocial support within HIV services as a priority. This promotes holistic care, addressing mental and physical health needs together, reducing stigma, and improving treatment adherence for people living with HIV. We must continue these conversations to raise awareness and combat stigma." ; "Integrating HIV and mental health services, along with other interventions, using a human-centered approach and linking social protection services for people living with HIV and other vulnerable populations, is critically important," Shangula stressed.

a6622.speaker: Kalumbi Shangula, Namibian Health Minister
a6622.name: Kalumbi Shangula
a6622.title: Namibian Health Minister
a6622.speech: Highlighted the nation's progress: "Statistics show that 93% of people living with HIV in Namibia have been tested and know their status. Of those, 95% are receiving free antiretroviral therapy (ARVs) provided by the government, and 98% of those on ARVs are virally suppressed. Our commitment to mental wellness as part of HIV care includes improving access to services, reducing stigma, strengthening support networks, and ensuring integrated care. The Ministry and Government remain unwavering in our dedication to ending the HIV/AIDS epidemic as a public health threat by 2030."

a6622.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS) of Namibia
a6622.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS) of Namibia
a6622.speech: Marked World AIDS Day with a commemoration in Rundu under the theme "Take the Rights Path," calling for action to prioritize and protect human rights to achieve the shared goal of ending AIDS by 2030.

a6622.speaker: Cheryl Amoroso, PEPFAR Country Coordinator
a6622.name: Cheryl Amoroso
a6622.title: PEPFAR Country Coordinator
a6622.speech: Praised Namibia's efforts to bring health services closer to its people, underscoring the importance of accessibility and innovation in tackling HIV/AIDS and promoting mental wellness.

a6814.speaker: Jeune Afrique (ranking of the 500 top-performing African companies)
a6814.name: Jeune Afrique (ranking of the 500 top-performing African companies)
a6814.speech: The latest ranking of the 500 top-performing African companies by Jeune Afrique places Abidjan as home to 30 of the continent’s leading enterprises.

a6814.speaker: Moody’s
a6814.name: Moody’s
a6814.speech: In March 2024, Moody’s upgraded Côte d’Ivoire’s sovereign rating to Ba2, citing the “robustness of its economic institutions”.

a6814.speaker: Fitch Ratings
a6814.name: Fitch Ratings
a6814.speech: In January 2025, Fitch Ratings affirmed the country’s rating at BB- with a stable outlook.

a6814.speaker: Alassane Ouattara, President of Côte d’Ivoire
a6814.name: Alassane Ouattara
a6814.title: President of Côte d’Ivoire
a6814.speech: As early as 2015, President Ouattara emphasized the importance of private sector investment in transforming raw materials into finished goods, particularly urging the cocoa industry to move towards chocolate production.

a6814.speaker: Government of Côte d’Ivoire / President Alassane Ouattara
a6814.name: Government of Côte d’Ivoire / President Alassane Ouattara
a6814.speech: The government has pledged to address these critical issues, with President Ouattara affirming his commitment to halving poverty by 2030 through a strategy focused on economic inclusion and providing greater support for youth and women.

a6923.speaker: Authorities (Beira Central Hospital / health authorities)
a6923.name: Authorities (Beira Central Hospital / health authorities)
a6923.speech: Stress the need to strengthen the engagement of the whole of society in order to reverse the current trend of motorcycle accident admissions.

a6923.speaker: Placido Pereira, Secretary of State for Nampula
a6923.name: Placido Pereira
a6923.title: Secretary of State for Nampula
a6923.speech: Gave the assurance that the completion of the works on the Angoche Fishing Port in Nampula will allow the berthing of about sixty-five tuna fishing vessels and transform the district into a hub of urban development.

a6923.speaker: Provincial directorate of industry and commerce (Inhambane)
a6923.name: Provincial directorate of industry and commerce (Inhambane)
a6923.speech: Said the province could take in more than three billion meticais, with Inhambane expecting to market more than one million eight hundred thousand tonnes of various products in the present campaign, notably cashew nuts, coconut and citrus.

a6923.speaker: Rasaque Manhique, Mayor of Maputo
a6923.name: Rasaque Manhique
a6923.title: Mayor of Maputo
a6923.speech: Says that the disorder and dispute over space between buses and vendors at the Zimpeto transport terminal has its days numbered, and wants an urgent meeting with the company managing the public toilets in order to demand improved, quality services.

a6923.speaker: Isaias Mondlane, Chairman of the Board of Directors of INAMAR (National Institute of the Sea)
a6923.name: Isaias Mondlane
a6923.title: Chairman of the Board of Directors of INAMAR (National Institute of the Sea)
a6923.speech: Warns that illegal fishing is having a negative impact on Mozambique's economy, including a reduction of the workforce in the sector, and said that to strengthen maritime patrolling on the Cahora Bassa reservoir INAMAR plans, in the short and medium term, to use drones, helicopters and dogs in patrolling.

a6955.speaker: Aisha Ismail, university student in Hargeisa
a6955.name: Aisha Ismail
a6955.title: university student in Hargeisa
a6955.speech: "Donald is our saviour. He is a wise and practical man. God bless America."

a6955.speaker: Abdi Mohamud, data analyst in Mogadishu
a6955.name: Abdi Mohamud
a6955.title: data analyst in Mogadishu
a6955.speech: "I doubt Donald Trump knows what Somaliland is, never mind where it is." ; "I am spitting fire."

a6955.speaker: Project 2025 (Heritage Foundation roadmap document)
a6955.name: Project 2025 (Heritage Foundation roadmap document)
a6955.speech: Proposes "the recognition of Somaliland statehood as a hedge against the US's deteriorating position in Djibouti"; mentions only two African territories in its sub-Saharan Africa section - Somaliland and Djibouti.

a6955.speaker: Ali Mohamed Omar, Somali State Minister for Foreign Affairs
a6955.name: Ali Mohamed Omar
a6955.title: Somali State Minister for Foreign Affairs
a6955.speech: "Any move towards recognising Somaliland's independence would not only contravene Somalia's sovereignty but also destabilise the region by setting a dangerous precedent."

a6955.speaker: Ali Mohamed Omar, Somali State Minister for Foreign Affairs
a6955.name: Ali Mohamed Omar
a6955.title: Somali State Minister for Foreign Affairs
a6955.speech: Highlighted concerns about a possible repeat of the first Trump administration's decision to withdraw from Somalia most American troops who have been fighting al-Shabab, warning: "A withdrawal would create a significant security vacuum, emboldening terrorist groups and threatening the stability of not only Somalia but the broader Horn of Africa."

a6955.speaker: Aden Ibrahim Aw Hirsi, Somalia's then-Environment Minister
a6955.name: Aden Ibrahim Aw Hirsi
a6955.title: Somalia's then-Environment Minister
a6955.speech: "You are always going on about 'political bombshells' in your reporting. People here are talking about a political earthquake. This is far more serious. It is a tsunami."

a6955.speaker: Joshua Meservey, Hudson Institute (formerly Heritage Foundation)
a6955.name: Joshua Meservey
a6955.title: Hudson Institute (formerly Heritage Foundation)
a6955.speech: "The case for Somaliland in US terms is very compelling," he argues. "I think the question of recognition will definitely be discussed, although the guiding north star is what is best for US national interests in practical terms." ; Adds that the territory should be "rewarded" for adhering to democratic principles, not relying on foreign aid and having a small government.

a6955.speaker: Abdirahman Dahir Adan, Somaliland's Foreign Minister
a6955.name: Abdirahman Dahir Adan
a6955.title: Somaliland's Foreign Minister
a6955.speech: "If the deal is good for us, we will take it. If the US wants a military base here we will give it to them."

a6955.speaker: US-based Somaliland diplomat (anonymous)
a6955.name: US-based Somaliland diplomat (anonymous)
a6955.speech: "It depends how they sell it to him. They have to make it attractive; they have to seduce him."

a6955.speaker: Ken Menkhaus, US academic
a6955.name: Ken Menkhaus
a6955.title: US academic
a6955.speech: "It is very likely we will see significant shifts in US policy towards Somaliland and Somalia," he says. "Mr Trump has a deep suspicion of foreign aid, is sceptical about state-building and is a neo-isolationist."

a7004.speaker: Pam Bondi, US Attorney General
a7004.name: Pam Bondi
a7004.title: US Attorney General
a7004.speech: Announced that the Trump administration is offering a US$50 million reward for information leading to the arrest of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, and accused Maduro of conspiring with multiple gangs to bring guns and illegal drugs into the United States. "Maduro uses foreign terrorist organisations like (Tren de Aragua), Sinaloa and Cartel of the Suns to bring deadly drugs and violence into our country" ; said the Drug Enforcement Administration has so far seized 30 tonnes of cocaine subsequently linked to Maduro and his associates, nearly seven tonnes of it linked to Maduro himself, explaining that this represents a primary source of income for gangs operating in Venezuela and Mexico ; "Cocaine is often laced with fentanyl, resulting in the loss and destruction of countless American lives" ; "The DOJ has seized over US$700 million of Maduro linked assets, including two private jets, nine vehicles and more. Yet Maduro's reign of terror continues" ; "He is one of the largest narco-traffickers in the world, and a threat to our national security."

a7018.speaker: Tomás Matola, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Hidroeléctrica de Cahora Bassa (HCB)
a7018.name: Tomás Matola
a7018.title: Chairman of the Board of Directors of Hidroeléctrica de Cahora Bassa (HCB)
a7018.speech: “Despite the hydrological constraints, HCB, through judicious and careful management, managed to achieve in 2024 financial results worthy of note, being the largest in its entire history. Thus, on net income, the dividends of 52.55% approved by HCB’s Ordinary General Meeting stand at around 7.4 billion meticais. In particular, slightly more than 6.5 billion meticais will be channelled to the Mozambican State, which, together with taxes and fees, will reinforce the State Budget, necessary for the implementation of the country’s social programmes,” said Tomás Matola.

a7018.speaker: Shareholders of Hidroeléctrica de Cahora Bassa (HCB), Ordinary General Meeting of 21 April
a7018.name: Shareholders of Hidroeléctrica de Cahora Bassa (HCB)
a7018.title: Ordinary General Meeting of 21 April
a7018.speech: Unanimously approved the company’s management report and accounts for the 2024 financial year and the distribution of dividends of some 7.4 billion meticais; assessed positively other matters of interest to the company; congratulated HCB’s workers and the Board of Directors for the professionalism and responsible management that leads to positive results, while urging the strengthening of corporate governance standards.

a7092.speaker: Chimimba David Phiri (PhD), policy economist and FAO subregional coordinator for Eastern Africa and representative to the African Union and UNECA
a7092.name: Chimimba David Phiri (PhD)
a7092.title: policy economist and FAO subregional coordinator for Eastern Africa and representative to the African Union and UNECA
a7092.speech: Writes that as a region prone to food insecurity and recurrent droughts, the COVID-19 pandemic brings with it an unprecedented challenge to the food and nutrition security of many smallholder farmers and population groups dependant on daily labour and movement for livelihood and income ; Notes that the increasing number of confirmed cases in Africa is of grave concern considering that the continent has fragile health systems and a high prevalence of HIV, TB and malnutrition, and that the current situation in Eastern Africa is exacerbated by the ongoing desert locust outbreak, with COVID-19 hampering efforts to curb the locusts by straining the supply chains that assure the delivery of pesticides ; Recommends that countries put in place robust policies and strategies to support agricultural production and maintain critical supply chains, lifesaving social protection schemes, adjusted school meal programmes, access for farmers to inputs, open trade among countries, stronger policy advocacy, data collection and sharing, measures on strategic grain reserves and food banks, and instruments for countries to access resources from multilateral financial institutions ; Argues it is critical that donor countries ensure continued delivery of humanitarian and development assistance where food insecurity is already high, and that regional and cross-country cooperation be strengthened, since all actors need to act now before the pandemic and other food security threats expose millions to hunger and malnutrition in East Africa.

a7092.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) food and agriculture policy decision analysis tool
a7092.name: Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) food and agriculture policy decision analysis tool
a7092.speech: Cited as having been critical to responding to the 2007-2008 food crisis; using the tool, FAO continues to collect, register, classify and analyse policy information.

a7130.speaker: Dieudonne Dahoun, National Coordinator of the PCCI (Integrated Competitiveness and Growth Project)
a7130.name: Dieudonne Dahoun
a7130.title: National Coordinator of the PCCI (Integrated Competitiveness and Growth Project)
a7130.speech: Said the competition is a response to the concerns of entrepreneurs whose projects are often either poorly designed, or lacking business plans, or discriminated against on the basis of subjective criteria; he recalled the selection criteria and the merits of the recipients, and welcomed the success of the initiative, which demonstrates its full relevance.

a7130.speaker: Didier Acouetey, member of the PCCI Advisory Committee
a7130.name: Didier Acouetey
a7130.title: member of the PCCI Advisory Committee
a7130.speech: Thanked those who set up the programme and congratulated the winners, whom he hopes will be active promoters of Benin's integrated growth through their SMEs, which represent 90% of the private sector and can be real sources of jobs for young people; even if the funds allocated to them under the programme are below most of their expectations, he has no doubt that they will be of great use and that the winners will even succeed in raising funds from banking institutions, in order to meet the challenge of creating thousands of jobs.

a7130.speaker: Dieudonne Alladjodjo and Pulcherie Ablawa Aholou, on behalf of the award winners
a7130.name: Dieudonne Alladjodjo and Pulcherie Ablawa Aholou
a7130.title: on behalf of the award winners
a7130.speech: Expressed their gratitude to the organisers for this business plan competition organised in a transparent manner, which allowed the winners to benefit from capacity building, leading to greater turnover and the recruitment of new employees; they promised to stay the course after being brought into the spotlight by the project by going out to conquer other markets, and recommended that the programme be maintained so that other SME promoters can benefit from it.

a7130.speaker: Pocoun Dame Kombienou, Minister of Industry and Trade
a7130.name: Pocoun Dame Kombienou
a7130.title: Minister of Industry and Trade
a7130.speech: Remarked that the competition came at a time when the government is making great efforts to offer good solutions to the problem of youth unemployment; the initiative is part of an international dynamic, he assured, invoking the approach of the Tony Elumelu Foundation's programme, and the competition is part of putting in place innovative solutions for young people, proof of the government's willingness to motivate and encourage economic operators to create wealth in order to build a strong economy based on the principle of public-private partnership.

a7130.speaker: Katrina Sharkey, World Bank Resident Representative in Benin
a7130.name: Katrina Sharkey
a7130.title: World Bank Resident Representative in Benin
a7130.speech: Welcomed the completion of this process, financed by her institution to the tune of 25 million US dollars; while the current growth rate is insufficient to significantly reduce poverty and provide work for the 100,000 new job seekers each year, she noted that Benin has enormous economic potential that needs to be developed and unique comparative advantages in a number of value chains capable of generating growth and contributing to job creation.

a7130.speaker: Lionel Zinsou, Prime Minister of Benin
a7130.name: Lionel Zinsou
a7130.title: Prime Minister of Benin
a7130.speech: Expressed his joy and thanked all the organisers; drawing on the experiences of entrepreneurs who started from, if not nothing, then at least as though on an adventure, he taught the harshness of the task as well as its exhilarating side, to reassure the winners and encourage them to persevere, indicating that everything remains to be built in most sub-Saharan African countries and that entrepreneurship is the driving force; offering advice drawn from the experience of developed countries, he suggested that efforts should ultimately aim at building roads, energy infrastructure and drinking water facilities and at developing agriculture, and that in any case growth must follow because runaway demography does not allow job seekers to be absorbed.

a7202.speaker: UNHCR (United Nations Refugee Agency)
a7202.name: UNHCR (United Nations Refugee Agency)
a7202.speech: Warned that more than 11 million people forced to flee their countries risk losing aid crucial to their survival this year because of significant cuts in funding by donor countries, in particular the United States of America - about one third of the population UNHCR supports; last year the agency supported 36 million people in 135 countries, a number expected to fall drastically, with the Chad and Sudan regions among the most affected.

a7202.speaker: Displaced Sudanese in refugee camps
a7202.name: Displaced Sudanese in refugee camps
a7202.speech: Say that life is very difficult and that shelter is a luxury, in a context in which humanitarian aid organizations have very little to distribute.

a7500.speaker: Augustine Samba Ndiaye, independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.name: Augustine Samba Ndiaye
a7500.title: independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.speech: Fakt is an initiative dedicated to educating and raising the awareness of young people in the face of the challenges of disinformation. It is a blog. "On our blog, we offer articles and practical advice to help young people better understand and counter the mechanisms of manipulation that proliferate online. We cover themes such as disinformation, press freedom and the impact of artificial intelligence on the spread of false information." ; "Through Fakt, we aim to bring together a proactive and enlightened community, capable of discernment and vigilance in a constantly evolving media landscape. Our prospects are ambitious. We want to strengthen young people's critical thinking and give them the tools they need to inform themselves responsibly." ; "My objective is to make African youth aware of the dangers of false information and to strengthen their critical thinking through varied educational content (articles, videos, infographics, podcasts...) distributed on a blog and various social networks (Facebook, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, TikTok). I want to offer young people concrete tools and reference points in a media environment saturated with false information."

a7500.speaker: Augustine Samba Ndiaye, independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.name: Augustine Samba Ndiaye
a7500.title: independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.speech: "I work closely with African fact-checkers including, among others, Azil Momar Lo of Africa Check, Blaise Pascal Andzongo, Andre Mpoudi and Fabrice Makem of Eduk-Media, Kaberu Tairu of Cellule Anti Fake News and Badal Fohmoh of Class Pro, to set up joint projects that respond to the local challenges of disinformation. In parallel, I am developing a Media and Information Literacy (MIL) kit intended for schools to help young people better understand and verify information." ; "In the coming months, I intend to further develop the initiative's YouTube channel as well as the TikTok account, incorporating podcasts and interactive formats. My objective remains to reach a wider audience by diversifying formats to adapt to young people's digital habits. Through this initiative, I want to be a reliable and accessible resource for young people, helping them to better navigate the flood of information to which they are exposed."

a7500.speaker: Augustine Samba Ndiaye, independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.name: Augustine Samba Ndiaye
a7500.title: independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.speech: On the risk factors in African elections: "Disinformation represents a considerable risk during elections in Africa. On the one hand, political instability creates fertile ground for information manipulation campaigns and, on the other, social networks, where information circulates rapidly and without control, facilitate the spread of false news and consequently the confusion of voters." ; "A particularly worrying aspect is the impact of foreign disinformation campaigns which exploit the vulnerabilities of young Africans to influence public opinion and sow division. These campaigns, often led by outside actors, use sophisticated tactics such as astroturfing, deepfakes and amplification via trolls. For example, during the 2024 presidential election in Senegal, a disinformation campaign circulated on Twitter, relaying a misleading narrative about Franco-Senegalese relations. Similar images and texts were spread by English-language accounts relaying an alleged speech by President Bassirou Diomaye Faye in which he asked France to leave Senegal. The technique used to attribute this fictitious speech to the Senegalese head of state was the deepfake. Likewise, elements such as an alleged rapprochement between Senegal and certain foreign powers, notably Russia, or with the Confederation of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), were amplified by disinformation campaigns. The manipulation of public perceptions is a tactic used to sow confusion among citizens. In this context, heightened vigilance and collective mobilisation against disinformation are crucial, because these manipulations feed rumours of political interference and conspiracy theories."

a7500.speaker: Augustine Samba Ndiaye, independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.name: Augustine Samba Ndiaye
a7500.title: independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.speech: On successful fact-checking responses: "In order to counter this trend, several fact-checking actions have been carried out successfully. In the run-up to the 2024 Senegalese elections, Africa Check played a key role in identifying and exposing the false information circulating on social networks. To return to the case of the presidential election in Senegal, ahead of the vote the #SaytuSEN2024 fact-checking alliance was launched, initiated by Africa Check and bringing together several media outlets and platforms. Before the first round of 24 March 2024, the Alliance's X account had already identified and debunked several pieces of false information, such as fake media front pages, fake polls, fake statements by influential figures and rumours of fake political defections. By analysing and verifying information published online, #SaytuSEN2024 debunked several fake polls and fake campaign images circulating on social networks. These actions made it possible to re-establish the facts and to publish fact-checking articles." ; "As social media have become increasingly dominant information channels, it is essential to develop collective vigilance in the face of these phenomena. One of the most effective means of combating disinformation is media and information literacy (MIL). Training citizens to identify reliable information and to develop critical thinking is becoming an indispensable lever for countering this phenomenon. Young people in particular must be made aware of the techniques used to manipulate information and be equipped to face these challenges."

a7500.speaker: Augustine Samba Ndiaye, independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.name: Augustine Samba Ndiaye
a7500.title: independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.speech: On whether fact-checking is a panacea: "Fact-checking is crucial but it cannot on its own stem the phenomenon of disinformation, especially during election periods. In this period, and generally speaking, false information serves to influence opinions. Thus, all actors have a role to play in reducing the impact of disinformation in electoral processes and ensuring the integrity of information: journalists must rigorously check the facts and make the public aware of verification methods; politicians have a responsibility to adopt transparent communication and to refrain from spreading dubious information; NGOs must raise citizens' awareness and strengthen media and information literacy to help them recognise false information; citizens, by developing their critical thinking and checking their sources, can be barriers against disinformation. Everyone must become an actor of vigilance in order to counter rumours and misleading information. In summary, while fact-checking is a crucial weapon against disinformation, it can only be effective within the framework of collective action. It is essential that everyone, at their own level, invest in promoting the truth."

a7500.speaker: Augustine Samba Ndiaye, independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.name: Augustine Samba Ndiaye
a7500.title: independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.speech: On Donald Trump's return and whether it is a failure for the press and fact-checkers: "The interest that Donald Trump's statements continue to arouse, as well as the adherence of some of his supporters to controversial claims, underline the significant challenges for the media and fact-checkers. These professionals play an essential role in society by providing verified and accessible information, thereby allowing citizens to form their own opinions on the basis of facts. In a context where information circulates rapidly and is easily amplified by social networks, verification work is all the more necessary to guarantee that everyone has access to precise and reliable data." ; "It is however important to note that the reception of information, even verified information, depends on many factors. Individual perceptions, cultural values and social dynamics often influence the way information is understood and interpreted. The media and fact-checkers, by providing clear and verified elements, contribute to a better understanding of the facts. In short, the work of the media and fact-checkers remains crucial to ensuring quality information by bringing objective elements into an informational landscape where varied and sometimes contradictory information may circulate."

a7500.speaker: Augustine Samba Ndiaye, independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.name: Augustine Samba Ndiaye
a7500.title: independent journalist and founder of the Fakt blog
a7500.speech: On reinventing fact-checking and MIL: "To limit the impact of disinformation, it is essential to develop critical thinking from the earliest age, teaching young people not only to analyse and understand information but also to verify its veracity. This education must be adapted to the interactive and dynamic digital formats that young people consume, such as social networks, videos or online games, in order to make learning more engaging and relevant, or else to integrate media and information literacy into school curricula, for example, which would make it possible to train a generation capable of spotting false information and understanding the workings of media manipulation." ; "Moreover, the role of local communities must be valued. It is a matter of encouraging every citizen to become an actor by helping to report and debunk the false information circulating in their own network." ; "Finally, diversifying fact-checking formats is also essential. Beyond classic articles, short videos, infographics and even podcasts must be used to reach a wider and more varied audience. That is why I am currently developing my YouTube and TikTok accounts. By adapting messages to the greatest number, we increase the chances of reaching people who are more vulnerable to false information."

a7506.speaker: Zambian government
a7506.name: Zambian government
a7506.speech: declared a state of national disaster after the prolonged El Nino-driven dry spell and heat wave caused 35-60% of crop losses ; has restricted the export of maize and mealie meal (maize flour) as well as soya beans meal and cake due to a prolonged dry spell that will likely affect the harvest.

a7506.speaker: Oxfam
a7506.name: Oxfam
a7506.speech: According to Oxfam, over 6 million people in Zambia are likely facing acute food insecurity and malnutrition over the ensuing months.

a7506.speaker: IFPRI report
a7506.name: IFPRI report
a7506.speech: In Malawi, about 4.4 million people across the country are projected to be food insecure, requiring humanitarian assistance, according to an IFPRI report.

a7506.speaker: Food Security and Nutrition Working Group (FSNWG) report
a7506.name: Food Security and Nutrition Working Group (FSNWG) report
a7506.speech: close to 4 million people in Ethiopia are impacted by the failed Meher harvests, and 5.7 million people in South Sudan are at risk of crisis or worse (IPC Phase 3+ or equivalent) conditions.

a7506.speaker: FAO Food Price Index and International Grain Council (IGC) Grain and Oil Index (GOI)
a7506.name: FAO Food Price Index and International Grain Council (IGC) Grain and Oil Index (GOI)
a7506.speech: presented declines in all major grain prices driven by expectations of large harvests in Argentina and Brazil, along with counter-competitive prices offered by Ukraine and Russia.

a7506.speaker: Jonathan Said, Vice President, Centre of Technical Expertise, Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a7506.name: Jonathan Said
a7506.title: Vice President, Centre of Technical Expertise, Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a7506.speech: "There are many information products on food security out there, but we hope that the detailed analysis presented in our Food Security Monitor brings more value to you due to its unilateral focus on African agriculture, food trade, and food and nutrition security."
